## CI: AI supply-chain review of action bumps

`.github/workflows/action-bump-review.yaml` has a read-only Copilot agent
(`.github/agents/action-supply-chain-review.md`, pinned model, strict JSON verdict) assess the upstream diff of every
digest bump on `renovate/*` PRs – except bumps of the popular actions that gate on Renovate's minimum release age
instead (`.github/renovate.json`'s release-age rule: GitHub's `actions/*` and `jdx/mise-action`) – and post the verdict
as a PR comment; the job's conclusion is the check a later automerge policy gates on (shadow phase until then). The
Copilot CLI comes from mise (`[tools] copilot`, backend `aqua:github/copilot-cli`, pinned in `mise.lock`) – the mise
manager bumps it and the minor/patch automerge rule merges it like any other repo tool. Facts below verified against
Copilot CLI 1.0.112 (2026-11-16); CLI flags: [programmatic
reference](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-programmatic-reference), [billing in
Actions](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/copilot-cli/copilot-cli-in-github-actions).

- Auth env precedence is `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` > `GH_TOKEN` > `GITHUB_TOKEN` > stored login: a `GITHUB_TOKEN` in the
  environment that lacks the Copilot Requests permission silently shadows an existing login and fails auth. CI relies on
  this order – passing the workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN` bills Copilot CLI usage to the repository owner's Copilot seat on
  personally-owned repositories (no PAT needed).
- In `-p` runs every tool request that would prompt is denied. Exception: shell commands the CLI classifies as read-only
  run *without asking* – so `--deny-tool shell` (deny rules beat every allow rule and mode) is what actually closes the
  shell surface for the reviewer agent, alongside `--deny-tool write`, `--deny-tool memory`, `--disable-builtin-mcps`
  and `--disallow-temp-dir`.
- `--max-ai-credits` hard-caps a session's spend; its minimum is 30.
- `--usage-output-file` writes final usage JSON (`totalPremiumRequestCost`, `providerModelMetrics[].usage` with token
  classes) – the workflow includes it in the PR comment for cost calibration.
- Repository-level custom agents (`.github/agents/<id>.md`, id = file name without extension) are only discovered in
  prompt mode with `--trust-folder`.
- `--reasoning-effort` accepts none/minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh/max; Claude Sonnet 5.5 accepts `high`
  (smoke-verified).
- The compare API omits `files[].patch` for binary or oversized files (source: [compare
  commits](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/commits/compare-two-commits)): files without a trusted-side reconstruction
  are surfaced as explicit unreviewable notes and the agent's verdict rules fail closed on them.
- The reviewer input file is capped at 500000 bytes (`.github/scripts/review_input.py enrich` assembles it): the diff
  comes first and one that does not fit is truncated with an explicit marker, which the agent must treat as
  unreviewable; context sections (upstream commits with authorship and signature state, tag/release context with release
  notes, BASE-revision workflow files referencing the action, the PR description) are appended in that priority order
  only while the budget has room – an omitted section leaves a one-line note in the file.
- Files whose patch the compare API omitted get their diffs reconstructed trusted-side: the workflow fetches the old and
  new git blobs (one `git/trees/{old}?recursive=1` call maps the old-side blob SHAs; `files[].sha` is the new side's)
  and `review_input.py` inserts capped unified diffs into the diff phase – per-file cap 128 KiB with an explicit
  truncation marker, NUL-sniff binary detection, `*.map` skipped as derivative of the `src/` patches, at most 4 files.
  Verified against tj-actions/changed-files v47.0.1→v47.0.2 (the dist bundle reconstructs to ~107 KiB across 97 hunks –
  fits the budget) and nick-fields/retry v2.9.0→v3.0.0 (~1 MiB – truncates at the cap), 2026-11-17.
- Digest-to-tag matching uses `repos/{owner}/{repo}/tags?per_page=100`; its `commit.sha` is the commit the tag points
  to, so annotated tags match too (verified for both tag styles against jdx/mise-action and git/git v2.44.0, 2026-11-16;
  source: [list repository tags](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/repos#list-repository-tags)).
- Renovate's github-actions manager rewrites a digest bump together with the pin's trailing `# vX.Y.Z` version comment
  and touches nothing else in the file (verified on PR #29's diff, Renovate 44, 2026-11-16). The review workflow's
  tamper guard normalizes a pin whose ref is exactly a digest followed only by whitespace or the version comment on that
  basis: digest+comment rewrites of any pin pass, any other edit to the workflow – including a longer or floating ref –
  trips.

## CI: Branch protection and platform-native automerge

`main` is branch-protected with required status checks (no review requirement, admin bypass on). Dependency-bump PRs
merge via GitHub's **native auto-merge**: `.github/renovate.json` sets `platformAutomerge: true`, the repository setting
"Allow auto-merge" is on. Renovate enables auto-merge on the PR and GitHub merges it the moment every required check is
green on the PR head – merging does not wait for the hosted Renovate app's run cadence. The required checks are the
*only* merge gate in this configuration – with none set, GitHub merges auto-merge PRs without waiting for CI (GitHub
docs' own warning) – so the required set below must stay in sync with the workflows: renaming a job, adding an app (its
`Lint app <name>` leg), or dropping a check needs the same change in the protection rule.

Required set (contexts are the job `name:` strings):

- `Find apps`, `Mise check (lint + validate)`, `Device-visible app changes require a version bump`, `Initialize builds`,
  `Build gate` – unconditional on every PR. `Build gate` (builder.yaml) folds the conditional `Build <app>` matrix into
  one static context: required checks must report on every PR, the matrix only runs when init finds changed app files,
  and the multi-arch build is a real gate for apk-pin PRs – the per-arch Alpine index race can fail one arch while the
  other passes (§"apk package version policy"). It passes on `skipped`, fails on any other non-success matrix result.
- `Lint app hd-idle`, `Lint app hickory-dns`, `Lint app nfs-server` – the find-addons matrix is repo-static (three
  apps).
- Deliberately not required: `Action supply-chain review (shadow)` (path-filtered, shadow phase – see §"CI: AI
  supply-chain review of action bumps"), `Build <app>` (dynamic matrix names; skipped legs never report), the
  apk-bump/publish-reconcile/skills-update workflows (post-merge or scheduled only).

Protection specifics: `strict: false` – no "require branches up to date". With it on, every merge invalidates every
other in-flight PR, and each invalidation becomes a rebase plus a fresh CI cycle; without it, a PR's CI certifies its
head against the `main` of that moment and the merge lands on a newer tip. Accepted trade for dependency bumps:
file-disjoint updates re-validated against a slightly newer tip add no signal (per-dep rationale in renovate.json's rule
descriptions). `required_linear_history: true` keeps the `automergeStrategy: rebase` property (one conventional commit
per bump, no merge bubbles; GitHub replays the branch's single commit onto the tip at merge time).
`rebaseWhen: conflicted` keeps Renovate from force-push-rebasing behind-but-clean branches: green check runs stay
attached to the unchanged head, so a batch opens in one window and drains in parallel – the apk-bump nudge's explicit
`@renovate rebase` comments still force rebase when the Alpine index race requires fresh runs.

Schedules: `after 8pm on sunday` + `before 8am on monday` (12 h strip, Europe/Zurich, all managers incl. apk). The
hosted app's runs are irregular and `updateNotScheduled` (default `true`) suppresses branch/PR creation outside the
window, so a missed run pushes a whole week's bumps out by a week. Batch intent: PRs open Sunday evening, required
checks run in parallel, everything eligible is merged before Monday 8am. `automergeSchedule` stays unset ("at any
time"): a batch whose CI finishes after 8am should still land instead of waiting a week. When changing this setup, apply
the protection rule (and "Allow auto-merge") *before* flipping `platformAutomerge` on: with the config live first,
GitHub merges auto-merge-enabled PRs while the required contexts don't exist yet, and heads that predate a newly
required context can never report it – they must be merged or rebased before the rule applies.

`.github/workflows/action-bump-review.yaml` has a read-only Copilot agent
(`.github/agents/action-supply-chain-review.md`, pinned model, strict JSON verdict) assess the upstream diff of every
digest bump on `renovate/*` PRs – except bumps of the popular actions that gate on Renovate's minimum release age
instead (`.github/renovate.json`'s release-age rule: GitHub's `actions/*` and `jdx/mise-action`) – and post the verdict
as a PR comment; the job's conclusion is the check a later automerge policy gates on (shadow phase until then). The
Copilot CLI comes from mise (`[tools] copilot`, backend `aqua:github/copilot-cli`, pinned in `mise.lock`) – the mise
manager bumps it and the minor/patch automerge rule merges it like any other repo tool. Facts below verified against
Copilot CLI 1.0.112 (2026-11-16); CLI flags: [programmatic
reference](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-programmatic-reference), [billing in
Actions](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/copilot-cli/copilot-cli-in-github-actions).

- Auth env precedence is `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` > `GH_TOKEN` > `GITHUB_TOKEN` > stored login: a `GITHUB_TOKEN` in the
  environment that lacks the Copilot Requests permission silently shadows an existing login and fails auth. CI relies on
  this order – passing the workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN` bills Copilot CLI usage to the repository owner's Copilot seat on
  personally-owned repositories (no PAT needed).
- In `-p` runs every tool request that would prompt is denied. Exception: shell commands the CLI classifies as read-only
  run *without asking* – so `--deny-tool shell` (deny rules beat every allow rule and mode) is what actually closes the
  shell surface for the reviewer agent, alongside `--deny-tool write`, `--deny-tool memory`, `--disable-builtin-mcps`
  and `--disallow-temp-dir`.
- `--max-ai-credits` hard-caps a session's spend; its minimum is 30.
- `--usage-output-file` writes final usage JSON (`totalPremiumRequestCost`, `providerModelMetrics[].usage` with token
  classes) – the workflow includes it in the PR comment for cost calibration.
- Repository-level custom agents (`.github/agents/<id>.md`, id = file name without extension) are only discovered in
  prompt mode with `--trust-folder`.
- `--reasoning-effort` accepts none/minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh/max; Claude Sonnet 5.5 accepts `high`
  (smoke-verified).
- The compare API omits `files[].patch` for binary or oversized files (source: [compare
  commits](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/commits/compare-two-commits)): files without a trusted-side reconstruction
  are surfaced as explicit unreviewable notes and the agent's verdict rules fail closed on them.
- The reviewer input file is capped at 500000 bytes (`.github/scripts/review_input.py enrich` assembles it): the diff
  comes first and one that does not fit is truncated with an explicit marker, which the agent must treat as
  unreviewable; context sections (upstream commits with authorship and signature state, tag/release context with release
  notes, BASE-revision workflow files referencing the action, the PR description) are appended in that priority order
  only while the budget has room – an omitted section leaves a one-line note in the file.
- Files whose patch the compare API omitted get their diffs reconstructed trusted-side: the workflow fetches the old and
  new git blobs (one `git/trees/{old}?recursive=1` call maps the old-side blob SHAs; `files[].sha` is the new side's)
  and `review_input.py` inserts capped unified diffs into the diff phase – per-file cap 128 KiB with an explicit
  truncation marker, NUL-sniff binary detection, `*.map` skipped as derivative of the `src/` patches, at most 4 files.
  Verified against tj-actions/changed-files v47.0.1→v47.0.2 (the dist bundle reconstructs to ~107 KiB across 97 hunks –

# Loaded Skill: ha-app-workflow (skill)

Change and release discipline for this Home Assistant apps repository – branching, Conventional Commits, lint gates, the single-version-per-branch release rule with changelogs, CI-as-source-of-truth, device-access policy, and the version-sensitive-facts rule. Use before making any change, commit, or release in this repo.

## Content

# Change and release workflow

## Before starting

- Check the current branch first (`git status`): **Always work on a branch named `agent-<topic>`**, create one if needed
  (based off of `main`, i.e. `git switch -c agent-<topic> main`).
- If work belongs on a branch but a stray commit already landed on `main`: move it
  (`git switch -c agent-…; git branch -f main <upstream-tip>`) and disclose it to the user.
- Never stage unrelated WIP: check `git status` before staging and add files explicitly.

## Commits

- Conventional Commits (`build`, `chore:`, `ci`, `docs:`, `feat:`, `fix:`, `perf`, `refactor`, `revert`, `style`,
  `test`); scope app changes (`fix(nfs-server): …`); one commit per logical unit.
- Final trailer line: `Assisted-by: Goose:<model-slug>` – the model name without provider prefix, e.g.
  `Assisted-by: Goose:glm-5.3-flash`.
- The commit-msg hook enforces the format; escape hatch `HK=0 git commit`.

## Before finishing a change

Run `mise run check` – lint plus validate; it is the same gate CI runs. Lint-stack details and scoped checking: skill
`ha-app-tooling`. Task usage: `mise run check --help`.

## App releases

- A working branch starting from `main` bumps `version` in `config.yaml` to a **single** next version (major, minor or
  patch by semantic versioning): the branch ships one version, not one per commit, and continuously expands that
  version's `CHANGELOG.md` entry until it lands on `main`.
- Transitory extra versions within the branch are fine where testing demands one (AppArmor profile changes are only
  re-applied on app *update*, never on rebuild) – squash them back into the single version (config plus one merged
  changelog entry) before merging.
- CI enforces the rule: `.github/workflows/version-guard.yaml` fails when device-visible app files (`rootfs/`,
  `Dockerfile`, `config.yaml`, `apparmor.txt`, `translations/`) changed without a version bump – the Supervisor's update
  model makes a no-bump change a silent no-op that only repoints an already-published version tag. Exception: if the
  base version's GHCR tag was never published (its release's build/publish failed), the guard probes GHCR and passes –
  reusing the version then repoints nothing; unprovable fails closed. Changes to docs-only files (README, DOCS,
  CHANGELOG, KNOWLEDGE, TODO, `.agents/`), the per-app `.dockerignore` (it shapes the build context but never changes
  the image the device receives), and repo tooling do not require a version bump.

## CI/CD is the source of truth for what gets published

- Pushes to `main` build and publish images (`.github/workflows/builder.yaml`). If CI fails, fix the repo, not CI config
  – unless the CI config itself is wrong.
- Builder caveats: the init job needs `fetch-depth: 0` – the changed-files filter otherwise only sees the tip commit and
  silently skips multi-commit merges, so use regular merges instead of squash merges.
- The app `Dockerfile` must not pull from Docker Hub at build time (rule and rationale: skill `ha-app-scaffolding`).
- The lint workflow runs frenck's app linter natively (pinned source plus pypi requirements), not via its Docker action
  (whose Docker Hub image builds flaked with 504s and 429 runner-pool rate limits).
- In `.github/workflows/`, match GitHub users and bots by immutable user id, never by `login` (root `KNOWLEDGE.md`
  §"GitHub Actions: user identity matching").

## Device access

Testing against the real HA device over SSH only on explicit user request; otherwise hand the user exact commands to
run. On-device procedures: skill `ha-app-device-testing`.

## Version-sensitive facts

Supervisor schemas, s6-overlay layout, HAOS kernel configs and HA docs change frequently. Wherever such facts are
written down (`KNOWLEDGE.md`, comments, skills), cite the source (URL plus version/ref). Before relying on them for new
work, re-verify against the latest docs/source.

## Design change proposals

When a fix reveals a design issue, diagnose hands-on first (strace, packet captures, a reproduction lab), then explain
root cause, options and trade-offs to the user before rewriting.

## Text files

Every text file ends with a final newline (the lint gate enforces it).

Markdown formatting conventions for this repository – panache owns all formatting, rumdl is the semantic second linter, and specific constructs break the toolchain. Use when writing or editing any Markdown file here.

## Content

# Markdown conventions

## Formatting ownership

- panache (`panache.toml`) owns ALL formatting: `mise run fmt` reflows prose to the 120-char width. Never hand-wrap
  prose – write naturally and let `fmt` shape it.
- The lint gate runs `panache format --check` and `panache lint` over tracked `.md` files – the lint adds semantic
  checks (references, heading hierarchy, …).

## rumdl

# Hickory DNS

## What it does

This app runs a DNS server on your Home Assistant device that answers every LAN device's DNS queries and resolves them
upstream over **encrypted DNS** (DNS-over-TLS, DNS-over-HTTPS or DNS-over-QUIC), with **DNSSEC validation** of the
answers. The point: point your router at the Home Assistant device once, and every device on the network resolves its
DNS through encrypted upstream connections – no per-device configuration, no plaintext UDP:53 queries leaving your home.

Under the hood it wraps the [`hickory-dns`](https://github.com/hickory-dns/hickory-dns) server binary in
forwarding-resolver mode: everything not answered locally is forwarded to the upstream recursive resolvers you
configure.

## Setup

1. Install the app. The defaults work out of the box: Quad9 (9.9.9.9 and 149.112.112.112) over DoQ (DNS-over-QUIC) with
   DNSSEC validation on.
2. In your **router's DHCP settings**, set the DNS server handed out to LAN devices to your Home Assistant device's IP
   address. Every (re)connecting device then picks up the new DNS server automatically.
3. Verify from any LAN device: `nslookup example.com <HAOS-IP>` (or `dig @<HAOS-IP> example.com`).

## Requirements and caveats

- **Give the Home Assistant device a static IP** (or a DHCP reservation). The router configuration points at a single
  IP; if it changes, every LAN device loses its DNS server.
- **Do not point the Home Assistant device's own DNS at this app.** The HAOS host needs a working DNS path of its own
  (the supervisor's DNS); pointing the host's resolv.conf at itself would create a resolution loop.
- **Only one program on the host can use port 53.** If you run another DNS app (AdGuard Home, Pi-hole, a dnsmasq app) on
  the same device, it cannot bind port 53 at the same time – pick one.

A relative `extends` is flattened (its rules are inlined), resolved relative to the config's own directory first, then the current directory. A user-global config with a relative `ignore-from-file`, at either the top level or rule level, is skipped with a warning: the path resolves against each linted file's directory, which a single migrated config cannot express. Make the path absolute or move the setting into a project config, then re-run. Absolute top-level paths are inlined as `exclude` patterns; absolute rule-level paths are retained. ## Deploy tasks: local builds and store-copy conflicts

With a top-level `image:` key set, the supervisor **pulls that image from GHCR** instead of building the app folder
locally – an image-based app never rebuilds from source (see the [dev docs on remote
development](https://contributors.home-assistant.io/apps/guides/testing/#remote-development)). The repo's device deploy
tasks (`deploy:local`, and `test:live` through it) therefore comment the key out in the *device-side* copy of the app's
`config.yaml`.

Two installations of the same app cannot coexist on one device – they conflict on the app's published ports. A
supervisor reject the update with `method 'manual' requires at least an address`), then `ha dns restart`.

The same mirroring also blocks on-device image builds (`deploy:local`) on devices whose only working plaintext resolver
is the device itself: the buildkit CLI container resolves the registry through a copy of the host's `resolv.conf`, and a
host-networked resolver answers container-sourced UDP queries with the egress route's gateway address as source IP
(per-route source selection), which DNS clients discard as source-mismatched – the build fails at
`load metadata for <base image>` before any `RUN` step runs. Substituting `172.30.32.3` as the host resolver triggers
the loop death above instead. Such devices can only take registry-deployed images (`deploy:registry`).

## apk package version policy

`mariadb`, `vlc`: bare `apk add --no-cache <pkg>`), while version-sensitive *cores* are pinned explicitly via

## HA base image: shell gotchas

Facts; the safe procedures (procfs writes, suppression of failed-redirection diagnostics, environment passing, PATH,
bashio stubbing): skill `ha-app-base-image`.

- **`echo`/`printf` emit a single `writev(2)`**: the base image's bash (5.3.9) implements the output of its `echo` and
  `printf` builtins as one `writev(2)` call, with the text and the trailing newline as separate iovecs. Kernel files
  that only implement the old-style single-buffer `.write` and no `.write_iter` (many procfs/sysfs transaction files,
  e.g. `/proc/fs/nfsd/*`) reject `writev(2)` with `EINVAL` – producing a misleading `write error: Invalid argument` that
  is about the syscall *shape*, not the written content. Callers that do a single `write(2)` (busybox `echo`, `cat`,
  many C daemons' own writes) succeed. (Which files this bites in a given app: the app's `KNOWLEDGE.md`.)
- **Failed redirections bypass the command's `2>/dev/null`**: a failed redirection is diagnosed by the shell itself,
  *before* the command's own redirections are in effect.
- **`with-contenv` wipes the inherited environment unless `S6_KEEP_ENV=1`**: the s6-overlay shebang helper runs
  `emptyenv -p` and then imports only `/run/s6/container_environment` (the variables the supervisor/s6 boot provides).

## Supervisor: DNS resolution chain (CoreDNS)

The HAOS host and containers resolve through the CoreDNS plugin, whose forward priority is: manual `servers` (the DNS
options), then `locals` (the host's NetworkManager/DHCP-learned DNS servers, exposed as `dns://<ip>` entries), then
CloudFlare DoT when `fallback` is true (`supervisor/plugins/dns.py::_write_config`, ref `6556811`, checked 2026-11-02).
`GET /dns/info` returns `data.servers`, `data.locals` and `data.fallback`; the device's own LAN IPs come from
`GET /network/info` (`data.interfaces[].ipv4.address` / `.ipv6.address`, CIDR-suffixed strings, v1 shape; the v2 shape
nests them under `state`/`config` instead). If the device's DNS servers include the device's own IP, the device resolves
through whatever app serves :53 on it – uninstalling that app (e.g. a locally installed hickory-dns) cuts the
supervisor's own DNS off mid-task, so subsequent registry downloads fail.

Setting a host DNS server equal to the CoreDNS plugin's own address (`GET /dns/info` `data.host`, `172.30.32.3` on
standard installs) is fatal: CoreDNS's loop probe detects the self-loop and the container exits (CoreDNS log
`plugin/loop: Loop` → exit 1). The supervisor raises the `dns_loop` issue and rewrites the config dropping both
`servers` and `locals` (fallback-DoT-only config, `supervisor/plugins/dns.py::_write_config`, ref `6556811`), but the
watchdog does not reliably revive the dead container – observed on-device 2026-11-12, where it stayed dead across two
network reconfigurations until `ha dns restart`. Since `locals` always mirrors the host's NetworkManager nameservers,
the CoreDNS plugin can therefore never be the host's own resolver. Recovery order after such an outage: restore the host
DNS servers (`ha network update <iface> --ipv4-method auto --ipv4-nameserver <ip>…`; omitting `--ipv4-method` makes the

Runtime semantics of the generated `/etc/exports` content (schema-side constraints are repository-wide: root
`KNOWLEDGE.md` §"Supervisor: option schema quirks"):

- The kernel keeps a single export cache entry per (path, client); duplicate lines resolve by *last line wins* –
  identical duplicates are noise, conflicting options silently apply whichever line is last (order-dependent). Hence
  duplicate (path, network) share entries are rejected: one option set applies per pair (the same path with different
  networks is legitimate).
- The per-share `fsid=` is assigned by config order (a counter): editing the share list renumbers the followers – NFSv4
  filehandles embed the fsid, so a renumber makes clients' old handles stale, including their recovery records after a
  share edit + app restart. An existing wart that only matters across share-list edits.
  filesystem's UUID, and filehandles keyed by that UUID are ambiguous once multiple exports share one filesystem (binds
  of the same fs) – they resolve back to the wrong export (mounts land on the read-only pseudo root → `EROFS` on write).
- The pseudo root needs no `crossmnt` (an NFSv3-era flag for seeing mounts beneath an export point): NFSv4 clients
  switch the export at mountpoint crossings regardless (`nfsd_cross_mnt` consults the export cache for any v4 client),
  and the pseudo entries mountd synthesizes carry `crossmnt` anyway.

## Grace period

Every restart cycle of the kernel server (`rpc.nfsd 0` + start) starts a grace period (default 90 s) during which
clients' write opens get `NFS4ERR_GRACE` and retry – writes appear to stall; a client-side write attempt in the window

# Loaded Skill: ha-app-markdown (skill)

Markdown formatting conventions for this repository – panache owns all formatting, rumdl is the semantic second linter, and specific constructs break the toolchain. Use when writing or editing any Markdown file here.

## Content

# Markdown conventions

## Formatting ownership

- panache (`panache.toml`) owns ALL formatting: `mise run fmt` reflows prose to the 120-char width. Never hand-wrap
  prose – write naturally and let `fmt` shape it.
- The lint gate runs `panache format --check` and `panache lint` over tracked `.md` files – the lint adds semantic
  checks (references, heading hierarchy, …).

## rumdl

- Second linter (`.rumdl.toml`, markdownlint-rules-rich); its own reflow is disabled (its fill state disagrees with
  panache's), so MD013 is a pure width check: code blocks exempt, lines whose only overrun is an unbreakable code span
  forgiven. panache's reflow breaks around struck spans, never inside them (it leaves a too-long span overwide on its
  own line), and MD013 does not exempt struck spans the way it exempts code spans: keep struck spans within the
  120-column width.
- Inline HTML is allow-listed per element, not per file (MD033), see `.rumdl.toml` for the currently allowed HTML tags;
  every other tag fails the lint, READMEs included. Reach for Markdown constructs (links, images, emphasis, code spans)
  before raw HTML. In tables, `table_allowed_elements` replaces (does not union with) `allowed_elements` (rumdl 0.3.1).
- rumdl never rewrites files: its fix allow-list is pinned to an inert `all` sentinel (canonicalization-preserved,
  verified through rumdl 0.3.1; behavioral canary in `validate/apps.py`). Formatting fixes go through panache
  (`mise run fmt`); non-format rumdl findings are fixed by hand.

# Loaded Skill: ha-app-workflow (skill)

Change and release discipline for this Home Assistant apps repository – branching, Conventional Commits, lint gates, the single-version-per-branch release rule with changelogs, CI-as-source-of-truth, device-access policy, and the version-sensitive-facts rule. Use before making any change, commit, or release in this repo.

## Content

# Change and release workflow

## Before starting

- Check the current branch first (`git status`): **Always work on a branch named `agent-<topic>`**, create one if needed
  (based off of `main`, i.e. `git switch -c agent-<topic> main`).
- If work belongs on a branch but a stray commit already landed on `main`: move it
  (`git switch -c agent-…; git branch -f main <upstream-tip>`) and disclose it to the user.
- Never stage unrelated WIP: check `git status` before staging and add files explicitly.

## Commits

- Conventional Commits (`build`, `chore:`, `ci`, `docs:`, `feat:`, `fix:`, `perf`, `refactor`, `revert`, `style`,
  `test`); scope app changes (`fix(nfs-server): …`); one commit per logical unit.
- Final trailer line: `Assisted-by: Goose:<model-slug>` – the model name without provider prefix, e.g.
  `Assisted-by: Goose:glm-5.3-flash`.
- The commit-msg hook enforces the format; escape hatch `HK=0 git commit`.

## Before finishing a change

Run `mise run check` – lint plus validate; it is the same gate CI runs. Lint-stack details and scoped checking: skill
`ha-app-tooling`. Task usage: `mise run check --help`.

## App releases

- A working branch starting from `main` bumps `version` in `config.yaml` to a **single** next version (major, minor or
  patch by semantic versioning): the branch ships one version, not one per commit, and continuously expands that
  version's `CHANGELOG.md` entry until it lands on `main`.
- Transitory extra versions within the branch are fine where testing demands one (AppArmor profile changes are only
  re-applied on app *update*, never on rebuild) – squash them back into the single version (config plus one merged
  changelog entry) before merging.
- CI enforces the rule: `.github/workflows/version-guard.yaml` fails when device-visible app files (`rootfs/`,
  `Dockerfile`, `config.yaml`, `apparmor.txt`, `translations/`) changed without a version bump – the Supervisor's update
  model makes a no-bump change a silent no-op that only repoints an already-published version tag. Exception: if the
  base version's GHCR tag was never published (its release's build/publish failed), the guard probes GHCR and passes –
  reusing the version then repoints nothing; unprovable fails closed. Changes to docs-only files (README, DOCS,
  CHANGELOG, KNOWLEDGE, TODO, `.agents/`), the per-app `.dockerignore` (it shapes the build context but never changes
  the image the device receives), and repo tooling do not require a version bump.

## CI/CD is the source of truth for what gets published

- Pushes to `main` build and publish images (`.github/workflows/builder.yaml`). If CI fails, fix the repo, not CI config
  – unless the CI config itself is wrong.
- Builder caveats: the init job needs `fetch-depth: 0` – the changed-files filter otherwise only sees the tip commit and
  silently skips multi-commit merges, so use regular merges instead of squash merges.
- The app `Dockerfile` must not pull from Docker Hub at build time (rule and rationale: skill `ha-app-scaffolding`).
- The lint workflow runs frenck's app linter natively (pinned source plus pypi requirements), not via its Docker action
  (whose Docker Hub image builds flaked with 504s and 429 runner-pool rate limits).
- In `.github/workflows/`, match GitHub users and bots by immutable user id, never by `login` (root `KNOWLEDGE.md`
  §"GitHub Actions: user identity matching").

## Device access

Testing against the real HA device over SSH only on explicit user request; otherwise hand the user exact commands to
run. On-device procedures: skill `ha-app-device-testing`.

## Version-sensitive facts

Supervisor schemas, s6-overlay layout, HAOS kernel configs and HA docs change frequently. Wherever such facts are
written down (`KNOWLEDGE.md`, comments, skills), cite the source (URL plus version/ref). Before relying on them for new
work, re-verify against the latest docs/source.

## Design change proposals

When a fix reveals a design issue, diagnose hands-on first (strace, packet captures, a reproduction lab), then explain
root cause, options and trade-offs to the user before rewriting.

## Text files

Every text file ends with a final newline (the lint gate enforces it).

# Open Home Foundation - AI Policy

We support using AI (i.e., LLMs) as tools when contributing to Open Home Foundation projects. However, you are responsible for any contributions you submit, and we are responsible for any contributions we merge and release. We hold a high bar for all contributions to our projects.

Our maintainers dedicate their time and expertise to reviewing contributions. Submitting AI-generated content that you have not personally reviewed and understood wastes that time and will not be accepted.

## Autonomous agents

**We do not allow autonomous agents to be used for contributing to our projects.** We will close any pull requests or issues that we believe were created autonomously, and may mark automated comments as spam. This includes contributions that bypass the provided issue or pull request templates.

## Communication on issues, pull requests, and code reviews

We don't mind if you use AI tools to help you write. However, do not have tools post unreviewed content on your behalf. Keep responses to the minimum needed to communicate your intent. We may hide any comments that we believe are unreviewed AI output.

If you are opening a pull request, we expect you to be able to explain the proposed changes in your own words. This includes the pull request description and responses to questions. If you use AI to help generate the pull request summary, you must review it for technical accuracy.

**Do not use AI to generate answers to questions from maintainers.** You should understand and be able to explain your own work. Using AI to improve grammar or clarity is fine, but the substance of your responses must be your own.

If you wish to include context from an interaction with AI in your comments, it must be in a quote block (e.g., using `>`) and disclosed as such. It must be accompanied by your own commentary explaining the relevance and implications of the context. Do not share long snippets.

## Limitations

- **Only `sd*` disks are monitored**: NVMe, SD/eMMC and loop devices are never touched (details in the
  [documentation](/config/app/f8b2d53d_hd-idle/documentation)).
- **Do not run other disk-monitoring tools alongside**: SMART polling keeps waking the drives.
- **Spin-up wear**: Shorter idle times result in more drive spin-ups, which eventually wear out the spindle motor and
  bearings; keep it at 3–5 minutes minimum (hd-idle's default is 10 minutes).

For usage, configuration and security notes, see the [**Documentation**](/config/app/f8b2d53d_hd-idle/documentation).

=== root DNS chain section ===
## Supervisor: DNS resolution chain (CoreDNS)

The HAOS host and containers resolve through the CoreDNS plugin, whose forward priority is: manual `servers` (the DNS
options), then `locals` (the host's NetworkManager/DHCP-learned DNS servers, exposed as `dns://<ip>` entries), then
CloudFlare DoT when `fallback` is true (`supervisor/plugins/dns.py::_write_config`, ref `6556811`, checked 2026-11-02).
`GET /dns/info` returns `data.servers`, `data.locals` and `data.fallback`; the device's own LAN IPs come from
`GET /network/info` (`data.interfaces[].ipv4.address` / `.ipv6.address`, CIDR-suffixed strings, v1 shape; the v2 shape
nests them under `state`/`config` instead). If the device's DNS servers include the device's own IP, the device resolves
through whatever app serves :53 on it – uninstalling that app (e.g. a locally installed hickory-dns) cuts the
supervisor's own DNS off mid-task, so subsequent registry downloads fail.

Setting a host DNS server equal to the CoreDNS plugin's own address (`GET /dns/info` `data.host`, `172.30.32.3` on
standard installs) is fatal: CoreDNS's loop probe detects the self-loop and the container exits (CoreDNS log
`plugin/loop: Loop` → exit 1). The supervisor raises the `dns_loop` issue and rewrites the config dropping both
`servers` and `locals` (fallback-DoT-only config, `supervisor/plugins/dns.py::_write_config`, ref `6556811`), but the
watchdog does not reliably revive the dead container – observed on-device 2026-11-12, where it stayed dead across two
network reconfigurations until `ha dns restart`. Since `locals` always mirrors the host's NetworkManager nameservers,
the CoreDNS plugin can therefore never be the host's own resolver. Recovery order after such an outage: restore the host
DNS servers (`ha network update <iface> --ipv4-method auto --ipv4-nameserver <ip>…`; omitting `--ipv4-method` defaults
the update to static method `manual`, which NetworkManager rejects for an address-less profile), then `ha dns restart`.

The same mirroring also blocks on-device image builds (`deploy:local`) on devices whose only working plaintext resolver
is the device itself: the buildkit CLI container resolves the registry through a copy of the host's `resolv.conf`, and a
host-networked resolver answers container-sourced UDP queries with the egress route's gateway address as source IP
(per-route source selection), which DNS clients discard as source-mismatched – the build fails at
`load metadata for <base image>` before any `RUN` step runs. Substituting `172.30.32.3` as the host resolver triggers
the loop death above instead. Such devices can only take registry-deployed images (`deploy:registry`).

### Hotplug behavior

Drives are granted device access dynamically by the supervisor – including when re-attached later, without an app
restart. A drive that is detached when the app starts is passed to hd-idle for runtime resolution (by-id symlinks are
re-resolved once the drive appears) – and hd-idle applies its configured idle time to it immediately upon resolution,
without waiting for a configuration restart. The app also periodically re-resolves its configured drives: after moving
drives between ports or machines – which changes their kernel names (`/dev/sda`, `/dev/sdb`, ...) – hd-idle is restarted
automatically with the updated configuration (within about half a minute); no manual restart is needed.

## Activity log and debugging

Spin-down/spin-up events always appear in the app log. **Debug mode** adds a per-monitoring-cycle state dump for every
disk (useful when drives refuse to spin down); **Activity log** writes per-drive run/standby records to
`/data/hd-idle.log` – both field descriptions in the options UI have the details.

The lab boots app containers `--privileged` on the lab host, so host-side hardware state interacts with tests:

  unrelated IO is correct system behavior). Assert the event/transition – log lines, state probes right after a
  triggered command – rather than persistence of a state.

  drives; `smartctl -n standby` is designed not to). Device/bridge-specific findings live in the apps' `KNOWLEDGE.md`.

# Device testing

Tasks: `mise run deploy:local`, `mise run deploy:registry`, `mise run apply-options`, `mise run test:live`,
`mise run hd-idle:regen-drives.md`. Usage and flags via `mise run <task> --help` – not duplicated here. Device access

# Loaded Skill: hd-idle-runtime (skill)

Runtime architecture and procedures for the hd-idle Home Assistant app – the hd-idle-genargs/drives/pmfix/watch flow, the --check baseline replay, SG_IO privileges, drive-ID conventions, and restart semantics. Use before touching hd-idle runtime code, its s6 services, or when debugging the app on a device.

## Content

# hd-idle runtime

## Architecture orientation

hd-idle has no config file – every setting is command line (facts: `hd-idle/KNOWLEDGE.md` §"CLI-only configuration").
The app generates that command line from the app options and keeps it in sync with the hardware:

- `/usr/bin/hd-idle-genargs` – the shared generator, used by cont-init and the watcher. Full generation (default) reads
  the options, resolves every configured device and writes three files; `--check` replays the recorded baseline with no
  option reads and no jq (facts: §"hd-idle-watch design").
- `/etc/hd-idle.args` – one line: the daemon argv, word-split by the s6 run script (every token must be space-free).
- `/etc/hd-idle.drives` – hd-idle-pmfix's interface: one `<kernel-name> <idle> <command-type> <pm-flag>` line per drive
  with per-drive values (format and semantics: §"Drive-PM treatment"; system-disk exclusion rows use `-` as the
  command-type column).
- `/etc/hd-idle.resolution` – the baseline state file, written LAST (commit point of the three-file install).
- `/usr/bin/hd-idle-pmfix` – drive-PM treatment via smartctl (§"Drive-PM treatment").
- `/usr/bin/hd-idle-healthcheck` – the Docker HEALTHCHECK probe (stats file + daemon process; §"Daemon failure
  semantics").
- s6-rc services: `hd-idle` (longrun; its run script reads the args file and `exec`s the daemon, so s6 signals hd-idle
  directly on stop and its stdout – spinup/spindown events, debug lines – lands in the app log) and `hd-idle-watch`
  (longrun, 30 s tick). cont-init: `/etc/cont-init.d/config.sh`.

Drive IDs: the options reference stable by-id paths (the physical `ata-<MODEL>_<SERIAL>` link and the `usb-*` enclosure
entry); hd-idle itself only ever sees kernel names. Regenerate the drive cheat sheet with
`mise run hd-idle:regen-drives.md <host>` (writes `hd-idle/.drives.md`).

## Boot sequence

1. cont-init `config.sh` runs `hd-idle-genargs /etc/hd-idle.args` (full generation). Failure aborts the app boot; a
   missing args file afterwards makes the run script fail loudly (s6 restarts it).
2. `config.sh` then runs `hd-idle-pmfix /etc/hd-idle.drives` – non-fatal, the treatment is best-effort.
3. s6-rc starts the two longruns: `hd-idle` (the daemon) and `hd-idle-watch`.

## The change cycle (hd-idle-watch tick)

Why the watcher exists at all – hd-idle's `-s 1` never re-verifies resolved entries and the supervisor cannot help:
§"hd-idle-watch design".

1. `hd-idle-genargs --quiet --check` replays the baseline (file shas, system-disk set, per-device resolution outcomes):
   exit 0 = unchanged → next tick (no log output at all); exit 3 = changed (regeneration due); any other nonzero = check
   failure → log once, keep the current configuration.
2. On exit 3: full generation into /tmp candidate files.
3. If the regenerated args AND drives files match the installed ones, only the baseline state is stale (an interrupted
   install, or a resolution change that reverted): resync the state file only – no restart.
4. Otherwise install: copy the drives file to `.prev`, `mv` the candidates over args and drives, `mv` the state file
   last, run `hd-idle-pmfix <drives> --since <drives.prev>`, then `s6-svc -r /run/service/hd-idle`.

## Drive-PM treatment flow

`hd-idle-pmfix` runs unconditionally at boot and after every regeneration (a global-only gate could not express
per-drive switches; drives-file interface and why: §"Drive-PM treatment"); it skips pm-flag-0 drives.
`--since <old-drives-file>` restricts treatment to lines that are NEW or CHANGED (a flipped pm-flag counts as changed –
redundant-treatment risk: §"USB-bridge behaviors").

## Debugging playbook

- Which log carries what: boot-time configuration messages and the drive inventory (by-id mapping and first-partition
  labels; facts: hd-idle/KNOWLEDGE.md §"Drive inventory") come from the non-quiet cont-init run; daemon stdout
  (`sda spindown`/`spinup` events, debug lines) and watcher notices land in the app log – unchanged watcher ticks are
  silent. The optional activity log (-l) is `/data/hd-idle.log`.
- A drive detached at boot is passed through for hd-idle's runtime resolution and recorded as PASSTHRU in the baseline;
  the watcher restarts hd-idle once it resolves.
- Two by-id symlinks for the same drive with one detached at boot: genargs' duplicate-entry rejection fires every tick
  while the known-good configuration stays in place (§"hd-idle-watch design").
- A restart does not spin up drives in standby; idle timers restart (§"hd-idle-watch design").
- ata-path commands failing with EPERM: two independent gates must be open – `capability sys_rawio,` in BOTH profiles
  and `/dev/sd* rwk,` (§"SG_IO privileges").
- Power-state probes: `hdparm -C` wakes drives – use `smartctl -H -n standby` (§"USB-bridge behaviors").
- Manual single-shot: `hd-idle -t /dev/sdX` needs the full `/dev/` path and uses hd-idle's built-in defaults for command
  type/power condition (`scsi`/`0`; the app sets no global `-c`/`-p`) (§"hd-idle -t quirks"); in the lab drive it via
  `docker exec`.

## Extending

- Adding a per-drive option: add the schema field (optional-boolean shaping: repository-root `KNOWLEDGE.md` §"bashio
  option consumption"), read it in hd-idle-genargs, emit it as a drives-file column or argv token (verbatim values need
  the space-free check), and let the consumer (pmfix or hd-idle) decide per drive. Extend the genargs/pmfix decision
  matrix in the lab.
- hd-idle CLI/packaging: the Dockerfile pins apk package versions because genargs encodes the CLI – a package bump is a
  deliberate app release (root `KNOWLEDGE.md` §"apk package version policy"; release discipline: skill
  `ha-app-workflow`).
- Testing: the lab boots the full s6 tree and runs the genargs/pmfix/watch roundtrips, but the spindown smoke test needs
  real spindownable drives – a device-side check (skills `ha-app-lab-testing`, `ha-app-device-testing`).

# Loaded Skill: ha-app-workflow (skill)

Change and release discipline for this Home Assistant apps repository – branching, Conventional Commits, lint gates, the single-version-per-branch release rule with changelogs, CI-as-source-of-truth, device-access policy, and the version-sensitive-facts rule. Use before making any change, commit, or release in this repo.

## Content

# Change and release workflow

## Before starting

- Check the current branch first (`git status`): **Always work on a branch named `agent-<topic>`**, create one if needed
  (based off of `main`, i.e. `git switch -c agent-<topic> main`).
- If work belongs on a branch but a stray commit already landed on `main`: move it
  (`git switch -c agent-…; git branch -f main <upstream-tip>`) and disclose it to the user.
- Never stage unrelated WIP: check `git status` before staging and add files explicitly.

## Commits

- Conventional Commits (`build`, `chore:`, `ci`, `docs:`, `feat:`, `fix:`, `perf`, `refactor`, `revert`, `style`,
  `test`); scope app changes (`fix(nfs-server): …`); one commit per logical unit.
- Final trailer line: `Assisted-by: Goose:<model-slug>` – the model name without provider prefix, e.g.
  `Assisted-by: Goose:glm-5.3-flash`.
- The commit-msg hook enforces the format; escape hatch `HK=0 git commit`.

## Before finishing a change

Run `mise run check` – lint plus validate; it is the same gate CI runs. Lint-stack details and scoped checking: skill
`ha-app-tooling`. Task usage: `mise run check --help`.

## App releases

- A working branch starting from `main` bumps `version` in `config.yaml` to a **single** next version (major, minor or
  patch by semantic versioning): the branch ships one version, not one per commit, and continuously expands that
  version's `CHANGELOG.md` entry until it lands on `main`.
- Transitory extra versions within the branch are fine where testing demands one (AppArmor profile changes are only
  re-applied on app *update*, never on rebuild; root `KNOWLEDGE.md` §"AppArmor: mediation and profile mechanics") –
  squash them back into the single version (config plus one merged changelog entry) before merging.
- CI enforces the rule: `.github/workflows/version-guard.yaml` fails when device-visible app files (`rootfs/`,
  `Dockerfile`, `config.yaml`, `apparmor.txt`, `translations/`) changed without a version bump – the Supervisor's update
  model makes a no-bump change a silent no-op that only repoints an already-published version tag. Exception: if the
  base version's GHCR tag was never published (its release's build/publish failed), the guard probes GHCR and passes –
  reusing the version then repoints nothing; unprovable fails closed. Changes to docs-only files (README, DOCS,
  CHANGELOG, KNOWLEDGE, TODO, `.agents/`), the per-app `.dockerignore` (it shapes the build context but never changes
  the image the device receives), and repo tooling do not require a version bump.

## CI/CD is the source of truth for what gets published

- Pushes to `main` build and publish images (`.github/workflows/builder.yaml`). If CI fails, fix the repo, not CI config
  – unless the CI config itself is wrong.
- Builder caveats: the init job needs `fetch-depth: 0` – the changed-files filter otherwise only sees the tip commit and
  silently skips multi-commit merges, so use regular merges instead of squash merges.
- The app `Dockerfile` must not pull from Docker Hub at build time (rule and rationale: skill `ha-app-scaffolding`).
- The lint workflow runs frenck's app linter natively (pinned source plus pypi requirements), not via its Docker action
  (whose Docker Hub image builds flaked with 504s and 429 runner-pool rate limits).
- In `.github/workflows/`, match GitHub users and bots by immutable user id, never by `login` (root `KNOWLEDGE.md`
  §"GitHub Actions: user identity matching").

## Device access

Testing against the real HA device over SSH only on explicit user request; otherwise hand the user exact commands to
run. On-device procedures: skill `ha-app-device-testing`.

## Version-sensitive facts

Supervisor schemas, s6-overlay layout, HAOS kernel configs and HA docs change frequently. Wherever such facts are
written down (`KNOWLEDGE.md`, comments, skills), cite the source (URL plus version/ref). Before relying on them for new
work, re-verify against the latest docs/source. Source reads are stamped `verified at <ref> (<date>)`, on-device checks
`device-verified <date>`.

## Design change proposals

When a fix reveals a design issue, diagnose hands-on first (strace, packet captures, a reproduction lab), then explain
root cause, options and trade-offs to the user before rewriting.

## Text files

Every text file ends with a final newline (the lint gate enforces it).

# drives are configured. Extend with device-specific drives + a short idle once drives are attached

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#MISE hide=true
#MISE description="⚠️ internal helper script"
# App-specific live-test hook for hd-idle, sourced by .mise/tasks/test/live.sh; hook contract:
# .agents/skills/ha-app-device-testing. HAOS ships no docker CLI, so container-internal probes
# (and the lab's forced `hd-idle -t` single-shot spindown) are not reproducible from here – the
# daemon's own log events are the strictly stronger end-to-end assertion anyway: a logged spindown
# proves the whole chain (device cgroup access, the /dev node open inside the container, the SG_IO
# ioctl under the device-enforced AppArmor profile, and the command execution).
#
# Hook-local contract:
# - LIVE_HDIDLE_LABEL_GLOB (env, optional, read by live_prepare under --test-options): a test TARGET
#   selector over filesystem labels. A disk is included only if ALL its labeled partitions match the
#   glob; disks hosting other labeled partitions are excluded explicitly; non-sd* disks are skipped
#   (hd-idle only monitors sd*); the supervisor's device validation is the final layer refusing
#   system-used devices. Each included disk maps to its preferred /dev/disk/by-id path (usb-* > ata-*
#   > wwn-*) and gets a 30 s idle (as in the lab fixture) so the daemon exercises its natural spindown
#   path within the check window; the FIRST discovered drive additionally opts out of the drive-PM
#   treatment (keep_drive_pm=true), exercised end to end (asserted in live_runtime_check).
#   Without the variable, the repo's test options file (a safe no-op: no drives) is applied unchanged. A
#   match-everything glob includes every labeled disk – choose it deliberately.
# - LIVE_HDIDLE_DISKS_JSON (set by live_prepare): JSON object mapping the disks' kernel names to
#   {label, device}; drives the per-drive assertions in live_runtime_check().
#
# The label walk only sees labeled filesystems: the glob is a test TARGET selector, not a safety
# boundary by itself (a disk whose partitions are all unlabeled is invisible). Never run with a loose
# glob on a device whose important data lives on unlabeled partitions.

# shellcheck disable=SC2029  # remote commands intentionally embed client-side values
# shellcheck disable=SC2034  # LIVE_* are the harness contract variables

live_prepare() {
  [ "${LIVE_HDIDLE_LABEL_GLOB:-}" != "" ] || return 0
  local glob="$LIVE_HDIDLE_LABEL_GLOB" raw kind name disk rank lb byid
  local -A disk_labels=() disk_byid=() byid_rank=()
  local included=() included_sorted=() labels=() ok
  local disks_json="[]" disks_map="{}" tmpfile pm_optout_disk

  echo "-- discovering drives on the device (label glob: $glob)"
  ## Partition -> parent disk via sysfs; by-id links -> kernel names.
  raw=$(ssh -n "${LIVE_SSH_OPTS[@]}" "$LIVE_HOST" '
    for l in /dev/disk/by-label/*; do
      [ -e "$l" ] || continue
      node=$(readlink -f "$l")
      part=${node##*/}
      if [ -e "/sys/class/block/$part/partition" ]; then
        disk=$(basename "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "/sys/class/block/$part")")")
      else
        disk=$part
      fi
      printf "label|%s|%s\n" "${l##*/}" "$disk"
    done
    for l in /dev/disk/by-id/*; do
      [ -L "$l" ] || continue
      case "${l##*/}" in *-part*) continue ;; esac
      printf "byid|%s|%s\n" "${l##*/}" "$(basename "$(readlink "$l")")"
    done
  ') || {
    echo "ERROR: drive discovery on the device failed" >&2
    return 1
  }

  while IFS='|' read -r kind name disk; do
    [ "$kind" != "" ] || continue
    case "$kind" in
      label) disk_labels[$disk]+="${name} " ;;
      byid)
        ## Preference: usb-* (the semantically clearest entry for USB drives), then ata-*, wwn-*, then
        ## anything else; ties go to the lexicographically first name (stable across runs).
        case "$name" in
          usb-*) rank=0 ;;
          ata-*) rank=1 ;;
          wwn-*) rank=2 ;;
          *) rank=3 ;;
        esac
        if [ "${disk_byid[$disk]:-}" = "" ] || [ "$rank" -lt "${byid_rank[$disk]}" ] \
          || [[ "$rank" -eq "${byid_rank[$disk]}" && "$name" < "${disk_byid[$disk]}" ]]; then
          disk_byid[$disk]=$name
          byid_rank[$disk]=$rank
        fi
        ;;
    esac
  done <<<"$raw"

  for disk in "${!disk_labels[@]}"; do
    case "$disk" in
      sd*) ;;
      *)
        echo "   (excluding $disk: not an sd* disk - hd-idle only monitors sd*)"
        continue
        ;;
    esac
    ok=1
    read -ra labels <<<"${disk_labels[$disk]}"
    for lb in "${labels[@]}"; do
      # shellcheck disable=SC2254  # the pattern is intentionally the unquoted glob
      case "$lb" in
        $glob) ;;
        *)
          echo "   (excluding $disk: hosts the non-matching label '$lb')"
          ok=0
          ;;
      esac
    done
    if [ "$ok" = 1 ]; then included+=("$disk"); fi
  done

  if [ "${#included[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "ERROR: no disks match label glob '$glob'" >&2
    return 1
  fi

  mapfile -t included_sorted < <(printf '%s\n' "${included[@]}" | sort)
  for disk in "${included_sorted[@]}"; do
    byid=${disk_byid[$disk]:-}
    if [ "$byid" = "" ]; then
      echo "ERROR: no /dev/disk/by-id link for $disk - it cannot be configured via the device option" >&2
      return 1
    fi
    disks_json=$(jq -c --arg dev "/dev/disk/by-id/$byid" \
      '. + [{device: $dev, idle: 30, command_type: "scsi", power_condition: 0}]' <<<"$disks_json")
    disks_map=$(jq -c --arg d "$disk" --arg l "${disk_labels[$disk]%% *}" \
      --arg dev "/dev/disk/by-id/$byid" \
      '. + {($d): {label: $l, device: $dev}}' <<<"$disks_map")
  done

  ## Per-drive keep-drive-PM opt-out: the FIRST discovered drive gets keep_drive_pm=true, exercised end
  ## to end on the device (hd-idle-pmfix must skip exactly that drive – asserted in
  ## live_runtime_check; the drives file is not reachable over SSH, HAOS ships no docker CLI).
  ## keys[0] == the first inserted (sorted) drive.
  pm_optout_disk=$(jq -r 'keys[0]' <<<"$disks_map")
  disks_json=$(jq -c '.[0].keep_drive_pm = true' <<<"$disks_json")
  disks_map=$(jq -c --arg d "$pm_optout_disk" '.[$d].pm_optout = true' <<<"$disks_map")

  tmpfile=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/hd-idle-live-options.XXXXXX")
  jq -n --argjson disks "$disks_json" '{disks: $disks}' >"$tmpfile"
  echo "-- generated test options (30s idle, scsi):"
  jq -r 'to_entries[] | "   \(.value.device) (\(.key), label \(.value.label)\(if .value.pm_optout == true then ", keep drive power management: on" else "" end))"' <<<"$disks_map"

  ## Must outlive the run: restore_options() re-reads it from the EXIT trap for its backup sanity check.
  LIVE_TEST_OPTIONS_FILE="$tmpfile"
  export LIVE_TEST_OPTIONS_FILE
  LIVE_HDIDLE_DISKS_JSON="$disks_map"
  export LIVE_HDIDLE_DISKS_JSON
}

live_runtime_check() {
  local disks_json="${LIVE_HDIDLE_DISKS_JSON:-}" logs tail_log disk label device byid inv_line
  local -A spun=() labels_by_disk=()
  local -r poll=15 hard_window=90 event_window=300
  local hard_pending=1 hard_deadline=$((SECONDS + hard_window))
  local deadline=$((SECONDS + event_window))
  local cmdline declared_managed declared_excluded expected drive_count spin_events=0
  local argv=() managed_arr=() expected_arr=() i

  echo "-- hd-idle live checks (event-based; spindown window ${event_window}s)"

  ## Only the CURRENT boot's log matters: `ha apps logs` serves the host journal (root KNOWLEDGE.md
  ## §"Supervisor: app and host logs are served from systemd-journald") and accumulates across app
  ## restarts within the host boot – this run restarts the app after applying the test options (a
  ## previous boot's "No drives configured" lines would defeat the assertions). Fetch a generous
  ## window of the current host boot (the default is the last 100 entries only), then cut at the
  ## last "Configuring hd-idle..." line (config.sh logs it at every boot).
  while :; do
    logs=$(ssh -n "${LIVE_SSH_OPTS[@]}" "$LIVE_HOST" \
      "ha apps logs $LIVE_LOCAL_SLUG --boot 0 --lines 400" 2>/dev/null) || logs=""
    tail_log=$(awk '/Configuring hd-idle/{buf=""} {buf = buf $0 "\n"} END {printf "%s", buf}' <<<"$logs")

    if [ "$hard_pending" = 1 ]; then
      if ! grep -q "symlinkPolicy=" <<<"$tail_log"; then
        : # daemon config dump not there yet - keep waiting
      elif ! grep -q "hd-idle configuration completed" <<<"$tail_log"; then
        echo "   FAIL: the hd-idle configuration did not complete (invalid configuration?); app log tail:" >&2
        tail -15 <<<"$tail_log" | sed 's/^/         /' >&2
        return 1
      else
        ## The generated command line must manage EXACTLY the discovered drives (by kernel name) – anything
        ## else would spin the wrong disks. -a entries with idle 0 are the system-disk exclusions
        ## (defense in depth); every other -a entry must be one of the discovered drives.
        cmdline=$(grep -m1 "hd-idle command line:" <<<"$tail_log" | sed 's/^.*hd-idle command line: //')
        if [ "$cmdline" = "" ]; then
          echo "   FAIL: no hd-idle command line in the app log" >&2
          return 1
        fi
        declared_managed=""
        declared_excluded=""
        read -ra argv <<<"$cmdline"
        for i in "${!argv[@]}"; do
          [ "${argv[$i]}" = "-a" ] || continue
          if [ "${argv[$((i + 2))]:-}" = "-i" ] && [ "${argv[$((i + 3))]:-}" = "0" ]; then
            declared_excluded+="${argv[$((i + 1))]} "
          else
            declared_managed+="${argv[$((i + 1))]} "
          fi
        done
        read -ra managed_arr <<<"$declared_managed"
        expected=""
        if [ "$disks_json" != "" ]; then
          while IFS= read -r disk; do
            expected+="$disk "
          done < <(jq -r 'keys[]' <<<"$disks_json")
        fi
        read -ra expected_arr <<<"$expected"
        managed_sorted=$(printf '%s\n' "${managed_arr[@]}" | sort)
        expected_sorted=$(printf '%s\n' "${expected_arr[@]}" | sort)
        if [ "$managed_sorted" != "$expected_sorted" ]; then
          echo "   FAIL: hd-idle manages unexpected disks (managed: ${managed_arr[*]:-none};" >&2
          echo "         expected: ${expected_arr[*]:-none}) - refusing to continue" >&2
          return 1
        fi
        while IFS= read -r disk; do
          [ "$disk" != "" ] || continue
          label=$(jq -r --arg d "$disk" '.[$d].label' <<<"$disks_json")
          device=$(jq -r --arg d "$disk" '.[$d].device' <<<"$disks_json")
          labels_by_disk[$disk]=$label
          ## The configured path must resolve to the host-discovered disk inside the container. The mapping
          ## line is logged only when the configured path is not the by-id link the inventory shows for the
          ## disk; otherwise the disk's inventory line carries that link itself.
          byid=${device#/dev/disk/by-id/}
          if ! grep -qF "Drive ${device} -> ${disk}" <<<"$tail_log"; then
            inv_line=$(grep -F "  ${disk}: " <<<"$tail_log" || true)
            if ! grep -qF "by-id: ${byid}" <<<"$inv_line"; then
              echo "   FAIL: no 'Drive ${device} -> ${disk}' mapping and no 'by-id: ${byid}' on the ${disk} inventory line" >&2
              echo "         (the configured by-id path did not resolve to the expected disk inside the container)" >&2
              return 1
            fi
          fi
        done < <(jq -r 'keys[]' <<<"$disks_json")
        hard_pending=0
        echo "   PASS: hd-idle daemon up, configuration completed"
        if [ "$disks_json" != "" ]; then
          drive_count=$(jq length <<<"$disks_json")
          echo "   PASS: hd-idle manages exactly the ${drive_count} discovered drive(s): ${managed_arr[*]}"
          if [ "$declared_excluded" != "" ]; then
            echo "   (excluded via idle-0 entries: ${declared_excluded%- })"
          fi
          ## Per-drive keep-drive-PM opt-out plumbing (boot log; the drives file is not reachable over SSH – HAOS
          ## ships no docker CLI): pmfix must have skipped EXACTLY the opt-out drive and attempted the
          ## treatment for every other managed drive.
          pm_optout_disk=$(jq -r 'to_entries[] | select(.value.pm_optout == true) | .key' <<<"$disks_json")
          if [ "$pm_optout_disk" != "" ]; then
            if ! grep -qF "Drive ${pm_optout_disk}: drive-PM treatment disabled for this drive" <<<"$tail_log"; then
              echo "   FAIL: no hd-idle-pmfix skip log for the opt-out drive ${pm_optout_disk}" >&2
              return 1
            fi
            if grep -qF "Drive ${pm_optout_disk}: APM disable" <<<"$tail_log"; then
              echo "   FAIL: the opt-out drive ${pm_optout_disk} received the drive-PM treatment despite keep_drive_pm=true" >&2
              return 1
            fi
            pm_skip_count=$(grep -cF "drive-PM treatment disabled for this drive" <<<"$tail_log" || true)
            if [ "$pm_skip_count" != "1" ]; then
              echo "   FAIL: expected exactly one hd-idle-pmfix skip line (the opt-out drive), got ${pm_skip_count}" >&2
              return 1
            fi
            for disk in "${!labels_by_disk[@]}"; do
              if [ "$disk" = "$pm_optout_disk" ]; then continue; fi
              if ! grep -qF "Drive ${disk}: APM disable" <<<"$tail_log"; then
                echo "   FAIL: no hd-idle-pmfix treatment attempt logged for ${disk}" >&2
                return 1
              fi
            done
            echo "   PASS: per-drive keep-drive-PM opt-out (hd-idle-pmfix skipped ${pm_optout_disk} only)"
          fi
        else
          if grep -q "No drives configured" <<<"$tail_log"; then
            echo "   PASS: no drives configured - hd-idle touches nothing (safe no-op options)"
          fi
        fi
      fi
    fi

    if [ "$disks_json" != "" ]; then
      while IFS= read -r disk; do
        [ "$disk" != "" ] || continue
        if grep -q "${disk} spindown" <<<"$tail_log"; then spun[$disk]=1; fi
      done < <(jq -r 'keys[]' <<<"$disks_json")
    fi

    ## All discovered drives have issued their spindown event – or (no-op options) the boot assertions passed.
    if [ "$hard_pending" = 0 ]; then
      if [ "$disks_json" = "" ] || [ "${#spun[@]}" -eq "$(jq length <<<"$disks_json")" ]; then
        break
      fi
    fi
    if [ "$SECONDS" -ge "$deadline" ]; then
      break
    fi
    if [ "$hard_pending" = 1 ] && [ "$SECONDS" -ge "$hard_deadline" ]; then
      echo "   FAIL: the hd-idle boot assertions were not satisfied within ${hard_window}s; app log tail:" >&2
      tail -15 <<<"$tail_log" | sed 's/^/         /' >&2
      return 1
    fi
    sleep "$poll"
  done

  if grep -qEi "error|denied|failed" <<<"$tail_log" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "   (note: error-ish lines in the current boot's app log:"
    grep -Ei "error|denied|failed" <<<"$tail_log" | tail -5 | sed 's/^/         /'
    echo "   )"
  fi

  if [ "$disks_json" != "" ]; then
    drive_count=$(jq length <<<"$disks_json")
    echo "-- spindown events per drive (daemon-issued, natural idle path):"
    while IFS= read -r disk; do
      [ "$disk" != "" ] || continue
      label=${labels_by_disk[$disk]:-?}
      if [ "${spun[$disk]:-}" != "" ]; then
        echo "   PASS: $disk ($label) spundown event seen"
        spin_events=$((spin_events + 1))
      else
        echo "   WARN: $disk ($label) no spindown event within ${event_window}s (drive busy/mounted? IO keeping it awake?)"
      fi
    done < <(jq -r 'keys[]' <<<"$disks_json")
    if [ "$spin_events" -eq 0 ]; then
      echo "   FAIL: not a single configured drive reached a daemon-issued spindown within ${event_window}s" >&2
      echo "         (all drives busy? command type wrong for these bridges? device access missing?)" >&2
      return 1
    fi
    echo "   PASS: $spin_events/$drive_count configured drive(s) issued spindown events"
  fi
  return 0
}

# TODOs

Open work items only (resolved items live in git history). Underlying technical facts and root causes live in
`KNOWLEDGE.md`, runtime procedures in `.agents/skills/hd-idle-runtime`.

## Tasks

- Monitor hd-idle upstream: v1.22 has no stable release (only a prerelease; Alpine tracks the tag); Alpine-side package
  updates are caught automatically by the apk drift check (`validate:apk-pins`, daily CI cron) and released per the
  repository-root KNOWLEDGE.md §"apk package version policy" (release discipline: skill `ha-app-workflow`). Upstream
  *behavior* changes (new flags etc.) are read and adapted when such a release is made; a future version adding
  per-device `-I` or a config file would also relax the option schema. Worth filing upstream: per-device `-I` would make
  the global-only limitation moot for mixed setups.

- Currently, hd-idle's `-s 1` re-resolves only *unresolved* device entries and never re-verifies already-resolved ones
  (`resolveSymlinks()` skips entries with a populated `Name`). A [PR](https://github.com/adelolmo/hd-idle/pull/141) has
  been submitted upstream to re-verify resolved symlinks each cycle and update entries whose resolution changed. Once
  this is merged and released, we can remove the app's `hd-idle-watch` service (see `KNOWLEDGE.md`).

- Drive-PM treatment blind spot (see `KNOWLEDGE.md` §"Drive-PM treatment"): a drive that reconnects under the SAME
  kernel name (its bridge power-cycled it) is invisible to hd-idle-pmfix's `--since` diff and stays untreated until the
  next app restart. Find a detection mechanism that respects the redundant-treatment risk (device-verified motor starts,
  see `KNOWLEDGE.md`).

- The `device(subsystem=block)` dropdown leaks partitions (by-id `...-partN` links) into the app config UI and users
  pick them, which our startup validation rejects with an explanatory message. The UX annoys real users (us), so we
  [suggested](https://github.com/orgs/home-assistant/discussions/5323) a finer filter upstream. Once approved, we could
  offer to submit a PR implementing our proposal.

- Upstream: file a feature request for per-drive (and/or global) disabling of the drives' own power management – the ATA
  SET FEATURES APM level and standby timer equivalents (`hdparm -B off` / `smartctl -d sat -s apm,off` and
  `-s standby,off`). hd-idle v1.22 only issues standby commands and has zero APM/standby-timer code (verified in
  `main.go`/`hdidle.go`); drives with their own power management active can wake themselves up again after an external
  standby command entirely invisibly to the host (no `/proc/diskstats` activity – observed on a test device for three of
  nine drives, 2026-10-15; an earlier setup.s fix for the same drives was disabling APM + standby timer before forcing
  standby). Note the empirical complication found on another host: behind some WD USB bridges the APM feature page is
  filtered out entirely ("APM feature is: Unavailable"), so the feature would need graceful handling of
  unsupported/filtered feature pages. Related: hd-idle's default `scsi` command type was a silent no-op (GOOD status, no
  drive action) for such a bridge under one host stack while `ata` worked – worth including in the request the
  observation that a "command failed/no-op" signal would help (hd-idle currently marks drives spun down even when the
  command has no effect).

- Design a better logo. Maybe a HDD that sleeps/snores ("zzzz")?

- Re-assess [`rust-idle`](https://github.com/Piezoid/rust-idle) as an alternative/supplement to hd-idle once a new
  version is released (if that ever happens – the last release is 2022-05). Facts below verified against the repo tip
  (commit 288d283, 2024-09-08) in 2026-10. The spindown command path decides most of the comparison:
  `src/sys.rs::spindown_disk()` issues a SCSI START STOP UNIT (0x1B, fixed power condition 0) via SG_IO on the
  `/dev/sdX` node, and that is its only spindown mechanism – the explicit "//TODO: implement for ATA/USB devices"
  comment sits right above it; there is no ATA path at all (no ATA PASS-THROUGH, no hdparm-style HDIO commands, no
  per-device command type).

  - Pros (honest): the one feature hd-idle lacks entirely – optional `syncfs()` + BLKFLSBUF of the drive's filesystems
    right before the spindown and/or on spin-up detection (the `s`/`S` config flags), flushing dirty pages so late
    writeback cannot wake the drive again; runtime auto-adoption of newly appeared drives with the current default flags
    (but per-drive configs resolve by kernel name once at startup, so a drive re-appearing under a NEW name drops to the
    defaults – including drives explicitly excluded with idle 0, a worse failure mode than hd-idle's stale-name behavior
    for our exclusion semantics); no `-I` equivalent at all (hd-idle's re-assertion flag is a wear generator on bridges
    where redundant STOP commands half-start the motor, per `KNOWLEDGE.md` §"Drive-PM treatment", so its absence is no
    loss); genuinely tiny (2 dependency crates, zero-allocation steady state, ~71 kB binary with nightly build-std per
    upstream claim vs the ~1.6 MB stripped Go binary – against the already-reviewed long-running footprint (the resident
    set is the watcher bash and the upstream Go daemon; RAM peaks are transient) this amounts to a small RSS saving at
    best); permissive MIT license (vs GPL-3.0-only) should forking ever become the path; its only command (START STOP
    UNIT) is in the kernel's read-safe list, so a rust-idle-based app would need no SYS_RAWIO (security rating +1) – but
    only as long as no drive-PM treatment (smartctl ATA SET FEATURES) is ported, which is precisely the feature this
    app's users rely on.

  - Cons (honest): effectively unmaintained (last commit 2024-09-08, a single v0.1.0 release 2022-05 while Cargo.toml
    already says 0.1.1, 3 stars, no open issues; the author frames the project as an exercise "to see how well rust
    fares"; contrast: hd-idle upstream is active, last commit 2026-06), with README-vs-code drift (the "monitors
    partitions" feature line is stale since the 2024-09-08 "track disks, not partitions" commit switched to disk-level
    counters); its SCSI-only path is exactly the one our testing found to be a silent no-op on some WD USB bridges
    (`KNOWLEDGE.md` §"Drive-PM treatment") while hd-idle's `ata` path worked there – on this app's primary target
    hardware rust-idle cannot spin the drives down at all; fixed power condition 0 (real SCSI/SAS disks need 2 or 3, see
    the hd-idle README); no activity logfile with running/stopped statistics and no single-shot mode (the lab smoke test
    and manual diagnostics use both); disk-level activity counters – the opposite of hd-idle's partition/dm attribution,
    chosen upstream precisely because monitoring daemons dirty disk-level counters (smartd/udisks false positives);
    tested on x86_64 only per README while aarch64 is the main HA device target; no Alpine package (AUR only), so the
    app image would have to build from source – a cargo toolchain in the Docker build and a crates.io supply chain
    instead of the apk-pinning + drift-check policy (nightly toolchain pin + `-Z build-std` per build.sh for the
    advertised size; a plain stable cargo build also works but yields a larger binary); no skew/suspend-detection state
    reset (after host resume it can keep believing an actually-spinning drive is idle – the same stale-belief class the
    WD-bridge findings document for hd-idle).

  - Current assessment: not worth replacing the hd-idle CLI here, and given the dormancy plus the SCSI-only path
    probably not worth a separate app right now either – the wins are marginal (sync flags, smaller daemon) while
    everything else is regression on this app's target hardware. Should it ever be pursued despite that, it belongs in a
    SEPARATE app (own config.yaml, device options, AppArmor profile), never as a CLI swap in this one – the app-side
    machinery (hd-idle-genargs/hd-idle-watch/hd-idle-pmfix) is built around hd-idle's CLI semantics. One thing survives
    this assessment regardless: the sync-before-spindown/spin-up idea is a legitimate hd-idle upstream feature request
    (could be folded into the upstream items in this section).

- Hermetic lab test for hd-idle-pmfix's `--since` decision logic (the treatment-success path is host-dependent, but the
  skip/treat DECISION is not): unchanged drives-file line → skip, new/changed line → treat exactly once, missing `.prev`
  file → treat all (pmfix logs every decision). A regression (e.g. in the line match) would silently re-treat asleep
  drives on every change tick – the wear-generating failure mode (`KNOWLEDGE.md` §"USB-bridge behaviors"). Mirror the
  genargs `--check` matrix in `.mise/tasks/test/lab/hd-idle.sh`.

- Device-side verification with real drives attached (the lab can cover neither half: it cannot simulate kernel renames
  – `.mise/tasks/test/lab/hd-idle.sh` – and has no drives): (a) extend `.mise/tasks/test/live/hd-idle.yaml` with
  device-specific drives and run the live hook through a short idle soak; (b) verify the watcher's core promise

121:## Device SSH: sessions run in the Terminal & SSH app
---
## Device SSH: sessions run in the Terminal & SSH app

- HAOS' host SSH server is not enabled by default (and would listen on port 22222); the standard SSH port 22 is mapped
  from the host into the running *Terminal & SSH* app ([`home-assistant/addons` `ssh/DOCS.md`
  §"Network"](https://github.com/home-assistant/addons/blob/master/ssh/DOCS.md)). An `ssh root@<host>` session therefore
  runs INSIDE that app's container: s6 is PID 1 and the session sees the SSH app's own PID namespace only.
- Consequences for live testing (the hooks' evidence model, skill `ha-app-device-testing`): processes of other apps are
  invisible – `ps`/`pgrep`/`pidof` list the SSH app's namespace, `/proc/<pid>` of an app daemon is unreachable;
  `netstat`/`/proc/net` reflect the SSH app's network namespace (with default port publishing, not the host's); there is
  no docker CLI. What works: the `ha` CLI (supervisor API), the `/local_apps` mount (app-store writes), `ha apps logs`
  and `ha host logs` (§"Supervisor: app and host logs are served from systemd-journald"). So: process/socket-level
  assertions come from the app's own log, network-level ground truth from client probes run on the dev host.

## Supervisor: app and host logs are served from systemd-journald

- Every `/logs` REST endpoint (`ha apps logs`, `ha host logs`, plugins, core, …) is served from the host's
  systemd-journald via systemd-journal-gatewayd (supervisor `api/host.py` `advanced_logs`; home-assistant/supervisor
  #4972). Docker's journald driver tags entries `SYSLOG_IDENTIFIER` = container name; the app endpoints query both
  `app_<slug>` and `addon_<slug>` (dual identifiers across the container-name migration).
- The default window is the LAST 100 entries (supervisor `api/host.py` `DEFAULT_LINES`). The `ha` CLI widens it with
  `--lines` (a `Range: entries=:-N:` header) and scopes it with `--boot <offset|id>`, where `0` is the current HOST boot
  – container restarts do not reset it. `--verbose` renders `identifier[pid]` per entry (the fastest way to see where an
  entry actually lives).
- One host boot's app log therefore interleaves every container boot (install, options changes, restarts).
  Per-container-boot segmentation needs an in-log anchor – the app's own cont-init banner line – and the anchor must
  track the app's actual logging: an anchor outliving its banner line silently broadens the segment to the whole fetch
