#!/usr/bin/env bash
#MISE description="Deploy an app to a HAOS device and run live checks against it (app hook provides the checks)"
#MISE depends="deploy:local {{ usage.app }} {{ usage.host }}{% if usage.replace %} --replace{% endif %}"
#USAGE arg "<app>" help="App to test (repo subfolder name)" {
#USAGE   complete run="git ls-files | grep -E '^[^/]+/config.yaml$' | cut -d/ -f1"
#USAGE }
#USAGE arg "<host>" help="SSH target of the Home Assistant OS device (bare host defaults to `root`), e.g. `root@homeassistant.local` or just `homeassistant.local`"
#USAGE flag "--replace" help="Forwarded to the `deploy` task: uninstall an existing repository-installed copy first"
#USAGE flag "--test-options" help="Apply the app's test options (`.mise/tasks/test/live/<app>.yaml`) to the device app for the run (backup kept, restored on exit)"
# shellcheck disable=SC2029  # remote/docker commands intentionally embed client-side values

set -euo pipefail

app="${usage_app:?}"

# shellcheck source=.mise/tasks/lib/ssh-ha.sh
source "$MISE_PROJECT_ROOT/.mise/tasks/lib/ssh-ha.sh"
ha_connect "${usage_host:?}"

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generic live-test harness; per-app checks live in .mise/tasks/test/live/<app>.sh – hook contract
# (live_prepare/live_runtime_check, LIVE_* contract vars): .agents/skills/ha-app-device-testing.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
slug=$(ha_app_slug "$app")
local_slug="local_${slug}"
host_addr="${host##*@}" # strip a user@ prefix

echo "== live test: $app on $host ($local_slug) =="

wait_started() { # wait until the app reaches a running state (60 x ~3 s budget for slow-starting apps -
  # hd-idle's concurrent drive spin-up; root KNOWLEDGE.md §"Supervisor: ha CLI HTTP client timeouts")
  local state=""
  for _ in {1..60}; do
    state=$(ssh "${SSH_OPTS[@]}" "$host" "ha apps info $local_slug --raw-json" 2>/dev/null \
      | jq -r '.data.state // empty') || true
    [ "$state" = "started" ] && return 0
    sleep 2
  done
  echo "ERROR: $local_slug is not running on $host (state: ${state:-unknown})" >&2
  return 1
}

# The client container runs with --network host, so its source IP is this
# machine's IP – servers with network ACLs deny mounts/connections from
# outside their configured networks.
device_ip=$(getent hosts "$host_addr" | awk '{print $1; exit}')
[ "$device_ip" != "" ] || {
  echo "ERROR: cannot resolve device address '$host_addr'" >&2
  exit 1
}
host_ip=$(ip route get "$device_ip" | awk '{for (i = 1; i <= NF; i++) if ($i == "src") {print $(i + 1); exit}}')

CLIENT_IMAGE="local/nfs-live-client:alpine3.24"
docker image inspect "$CLIENT_IMAGE" >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
  echo "-- building the client image ($CLIENT_IMAGE)"
  printf 'FROM alpine:3.24\nRUN apk add --no-cache nfs-utils\n' | docker build -t "$CLIENT_IMAGE" - >/dev/null
}

# shellcheck disable=SC2034  # contract variables are consumed by the app hook
LIVE_APP="$app" \
  LIVE_LOCAL_SLUG="$local_slug" \
  LIVE_HOST="$host" \
  LIVE_DEVICE_IP="$device_ip" \
  LIVE_HOST_IP="$host_ip" \
  LIVE_CLIENT_IMAGE="$CLIENT_IMAGE" \
  LIVE_TEST_OPTIONS_FILE="$MISE_PROJECT_ROOT/.mise/tasks/test/live/$app.yaml" \
  LIVE_SHARES="" \
  LIVE_SSH_OPTS=("${SSH_OPTS[@]}")
export LIVE_APP LIVE_LOCAL_SLUG LIVE_HOST LIVE_DEVICE_IP LIVE_HOST_IP \
  LIVE_CLIENT_IMAGE LIVE_TEST_OPTIONS_FILE LIVE_SHARES LIVE_SSH_OPTS

# Drop a previous app's hooks first: an all-apps run must not inherit the last app's functions
unset -f live_prepare live_runtime_check 2>/dev/null || true
hook=".mise/tasks/test/live/$app.sh"
if [ -f "$hook" ]; then
  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
  source "$hook" # sets live_prepare/live_runtime_check (optional)
fi

# --- apply test options (--test-options) -----------------------------------
if [ "${usage_test_options:-false}" = "true" ]; then
  [ -f "$LIVE_TEST_OPTIONS_FILE" ] || {
    echo "ERROR: no test options file '$LIVE_TEST_OPTIONS_FILE'" >&2
    exit 1
  }
  echo "-- applying test options ($LIVE_TEST_OPTIONS_FILE) to the app options"

  current=$(ssh "${SSH_OPTS[@]}" "$host" "ha apps info $local_slug --raw-json" 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -c '.data.options // empty')
  [ "$current" != "" ] || {
    echo "ERROR: could not read the app's current options on $host" >&2
    exit 1
  }

  # Backup next to the app folder (the next deploy wipes it with the folder). Keep a pre-existing
  # backup: re-running --test-options must not save the already-active test options as "original".
  backup="/local_apps/$app/.test-options-original.json"
  if ! ssh "${SSH_OPTS[@]}" "$host" "test -f '$backup'"; then
    printf '%s' "$current" | ssh "${SSH_OPTS[@]}" "$host" "cat > '$backup'"
  fi

  if [ "$(declare -f live_prepare)" != "" ]; then live_prepare; fi

  # POST body: {"options": {...}} (SCHEMA_OPTIONS wrapper); top-level keys override, missing keys
  # kept (objects merge, arrays e.g. shares are replaced)
  merged=$(jq -c -s '{options: (.[0] * .[1])}' <(printf '%s' "$current") \
    <(yq -o json '.' "$LIVE_TEST_OPTIONS_FILE"))
  result=$(printf '%s' "$merged" | ssh "${SSH_OPTS[@]}" "$host" \
    "curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer \$SUPERVISOR_TOKEN\" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      -X POST --data-binary @- http://supervisor/addons/$local_slug/options")
  if ! echo "$result" | jq -e '.result == "ok"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "ERROR: the supervisor rejected the test options: $result" >&2
    exit 1
  fi

  ssh "${SSH_OPTS[@]}" "$host" "ha apps restart $local_slug"
  echo "-- test options active; original options saved on the device at $backup"
  echo "   (restored automatically when this task exits)"
fi

# Runs on every exit path: leaving test options active is the worst failure mode. Define+trap BEFORE
# the checks – a failing check aborts under set -e and a later trap would never fire (device-verified).
restore_options() {
  local suspicious test_keys tkey
  [ "${usage_test_options:-false}" = "true" ] || return 0
  if ssh "${SSH_OPTS[@]}" "$host" "test -f '$backup'" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "-- restoring original app options"
    if restore_result=$(ssh "${SSH_OPTS[@]}" "$host" \
      "jq -c '{options: .}' '$backup' | \
        curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer \$SUPERVISOR_TOKEN\" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
        -X POST --data-binary @- http://supervisor/addons/$local_slug/options") \
      && echo "$restore_result" | jq -e '.result == "ok"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      # Refuse to apply a backup that IS the test options (a failed run may have saved them as
      # "original"): suspicious when every overridden top-level key carries exactly the test value.
      # Generic key comparison – no app-specific field name may be hardwired here.
      suspicious=0
      if [ -f "$LIVE_TEST_OPTIONS_FILE" ]; then
        test_keys=$(yq '. | keys | .[]' "$LIVE_TEST_OPTIONS_FILE")
        if [ "$test_keys" != "" ]; then
          suspicious=1
          while IFS= read -r tkey; do
            [ "$tkey" != "" ] || continue
            ## -n: keep the loop's stdin away from ssh (it would eat the remaining keys)
            if [ "$(ssh -n "${SSH_OPTS[@]}" "$host" \
              "jq -c --arg k '$tkey' '.[\$k] // \"<key-missing>\"' '$backup'")" \
              != "$(yq -o json ".$tkey" "$LIVE_TEST_OPTIONS_FILE" | jq -c .)" ]; then
              suspicious=0
              break
            fi
          done <<<"$test_keys"
        fi
      fi
      if [ "$suspicious" = 1 ]; then
        echo "WARNING: the device backup contains the TEST options – not applying them as" >&2
        echo "         'original'. Restore your real options via the app options UI; the" >&2
        echo "         backup stays at $backup for reference." >&2
      else
        ssh "${SSH_OPTS[@]}" "$host" \
          "ha apps restart $local_slug && rm -f '$backup'"
        echo "-- original options restored, app restarted"
      fi
    else
      echo "WARNING: restoring the original options failed: ${restore_result:-<no response>}" >&2
      echo "         The backup remains at $backup" >&2
    fi
  else
    echo "-- note: no options backup on the device; the test options remain active – "
    echo "        restore your options via the app options UI"
  fi
}
trap restore_options EXIT

wait_started

# The checks run against the app's ACTUAL device options, not the repo defaults (user-editable in the HA UI).
LIVE_SHARES=$(ssh "${SSH_OPTS[@]}" "$host" "ha apps info $local_slug --raw-json" 2>/dev/null \
  | jq -c '.data.options.shares // []') || LIVE_SHARES="[]"
export LIVE_SHARES
# No gate on LIVE_SHARES: that key is app-specific; each hook decides itself whether its checks fit
# the device's current options (nfs-server refuses without /share/nfs; hd-idle has no shares).
if [ "$(declare -f live_runtime_check)" != "" ]; then
  live_runtime_check
fi

echo "live test OK"
=== task def ===
lab
lab.sh
live
live.sh

# Home Assistant app: hd-idle

## Configuration

Drives are configured in the app's [settings](/config/app/f8b2d53d_hd-idle/config). Each entry in the **Drives** list
manages one drive; see the field descriptions in the configuration dialog for details. Saving configuration changes
restarts the app, which re-validates the configuration and regenerates the hd-idle command line.

### Drive list semantics

Every **listed** drive is managed with the settings configured on its own entry (**Idle time**, **Command type**,
**Power condition** – all required); an idle time of `0` never spins it down, and unlisted drives – including anything
that appears on the system later – are never touched. Only listed drives receive device access on Home Assistant OS,
which also keeps the system disk out of reach.

### Selecting drives

Pick each drive from the dropdown and select the **disk itself**, never a partition – see the **Drives** field
description in the options UI for the details. The by-id paths survive re-plugging and reboots even when the kernel name
changes.

On startup the app logs an inventory of all detected `sd*` disks and the generated hd-idle command line (one `-a` entry
per managed drive), so log lines like `sda spindown` can be attributed. Each inventory line shows the drive model, its
by-id path and – when set – the label of the drive's first labeled partition (filesystem label preferred, GPT partition
label as fallback; an unpartitioned disk shows its whole-disk filesystem label) – usually the name the drive carries in
file managers:

```text
# with command type `scsi`
[10:30:00] INFO:   sda: Elements 25A3 (by-id: REDACTED:0, label (sda1): my_movies)
# with command type `ata`
[22:49:21] INFO:   sda: Elements 25A3 (by-id: ata-WDC_WD160EDGZ-0AB4567_876543XY, label (sda1): my_movies)
```

### Drive power management

Drives – and some USB bridges – run their own power management that can conflict with hd-idle, so the app disables it by
default (the drive-PM treatment; every managed drive gets it unless it opts out). The per-drive **Keep drive power
management** switch opts individual drives out – switch it on for drives that must keep their own power management; its
field description in the options UI has the why and the details. A drive or bridge that does not support one of the
treatment's commands logs a one-time failure in the app log – harmless.

### Command types

The spin-down command is sent via one of two APIs – **`scsi`** or **`ata`**; the **Command type** and **Power
condition** field descriptions in the options UI explain both and when to use which.

### System disk protection

The drive(s) Home Assistant runs from are excluded from spin-down by three independent layers:

1. The supervisor never grants the app device access to devices the system uses – a configured system disk is rejected
   at startup with an explanatory message.
2. The app resolves the boot device (kernel `root=` parameter) plus all `hassos-*` partitions at startup and pins those
   disks to "never spin down" (logged as `Excluding the system disk(s) ...`) – this also covers USB-booted systems,
   where the system disk is an `sd*` disk hd-idle would otherwise monitor.
3. hd-idle itself only ever monitors `sd*` disks; system disks on SD/eMMC/NVMe are out of its reach anyway.

### Hotplug behavior

Drives are granted device access dynamically by the supervisor – including when re-attached later, without an app
restart. A drive that is detached when the app starts is passed to hd-idle for runtime resolution (by-id symlinks are
re-resolved once the drive appears) – and hd-idle applies its configured idle time to it immediately upon resolution,
without waiting for a configuration restart. The app also periodically re-resolves its configured drives: after moving
drives between ports or machines – which changes their kernel names (`/dev/sda`, `/dev/sdb`, ...) – hd-idle is restarted
automatically with the updated configuration (within about half a minute); no manual restart is needed.

## Activity log and debugging

Spin-down/spin-up events always appear in the app log. **Debug mode** adds a per-monitoring-cycle state dump for every
disk (useful when drives refuse to spin down); **Activity log** writes per-drive run/standby records to
`/data/hd-idle.log` – both field descriptions in the options UI have the details.

## Limitations

- **Only `sd*` disks are monitored**: hd-idle reads `/proc/diskstats` and only acts on SCSI-layer disks (`sdX`) and
  device-mapper devices attributed to them; NVMe, SD/eMMC and loop devices are never touched, and NVMe drives cannot be
  managed.
- **Do not run SMART-polling tools alongside** (smartmontools and apps built on it): their polling keeps waking drives
  and their activities are invisible to hd-idle. The upstream hd-idle documentation says the same about disk monitoring
  tools generally.
- **Spin-up wear**: frequent spin-down/spin-up cycles stress the spindle motor and bearings; keep idle times at 3–5
  minutes minimum (hd-idle's default is 10).
- **Ignore spin-down detection** is a global hd-idle setting and cannot be set per drive (upstream limitation), and can
  cause extra wear on some bridges (see its description in the options UI).

## Security notes

- The app requests `SYS_RAWIO` because hd-idle's `ata` command type uses SCSI passthrough commands (ATA PASS-THROUGH)
  that the kernel only permits with that capability; the `scsi` command type works without it. Drive access itself is
  granted per configured drive by the supervisor's device policy – the system disk cannot be granted at all.
- The hd-idle daemon runs under its own AppArmor sub-profile with all networking denied; it talks to no network service
  whatsoever.
- The app never writes data to managed drives: it issues standby commands and, unless a drive opts out via the **Keep
  drive power management** switch, ATA SET FEATURES requests that switch off the drive's own power management – but no
  data is ever written.

#!/usr/bin/with-contenv bashio
# shellcheck shell=bash
set -euo pipefail

## Drive re-resolution watcher (longrun service): kernel names are not stable across re-plugs and hd-idle's -s 1 never
## re-verifies already-resolved entries, so a moved drive would keep its stale entry until an app restart. Each tick
## replays the recorded resolution baseline (hd-idle-genargs --check) and only on a detected change regenerates and
## restarts just the hd-idle service. Problem, design, restart effects, failure class:
## hd-idle/KNOWLEDGE.md §"hd-idle-watch design".

## Poll interval (seconds); HD_IDLE_WATCH_INTERVAL overrides the 30 s default (the lab sets 5 s). Invalid values fall
## back to the default, floored at 5 s so a bogus value cannot busy-cycle the tick.
INTERVAL="${HD_IDLE_WATCH_INTERVAL:-30}"
case "$INTERVAL" in
  '' | *[!0-9]*)
    bashio::log.warning "Invalid HD_IDLE_WATCH_INTERVAL '${INTERVAL}' – using the 30 s default."
    INTERVAL=30
    ;;
esac
[ "$INTERVAL" -ge 5 ] || INTERVAL=5

ARGS_FILE=/etc/hd-idle.args
CAND_FILE=/tmp/hd-idle-args.new
## Companion files of the args file (derivation mirrored from hd-idle-genargs' companion_file; absolute paths here).
DRIVES_FILE="${ARGS_FILE%.args}.drives"
CAND_DRIVES_FILE="${CAND_FILE%.args}.drives"
STATE_FILE="${ARGS_FILE%.args}.resolution"
CAND_STATE_FILE="${CAND_FILE%.args}.resolution"

while true; do
  sleep "$INTERVAL"

  ## Detect (read-only): 0 = unchanged, 3 = changed (regeneration due), other = check failure; mid-run failures are
  ## nearly impossible by construction, so the keep-current guard is cheap insurance.
  RC=0
  /usr/bin/hd-idle-genargs --quiet --check || RC=$?

  if [ "$RC" = 0 ]; then
    continue
  fi
  if [ "$RC" != 3 ]; then
    bashio::log.warning "Checking the hd-idle configuration failed – keeping the current configuration."
    continue
  fi

  ## Regenerate from current options + current device resolution.
  if ! /usr/bin/hd-idle-genargs --quiet "$CAND_FILE"; then
    bashio::log.warning "hd-idle configuration regeneration failed – keeping the current configuration."
    continue
  fi

  ## Regenerated args AND drives still matching the installed ones = only the baseline state is stale (interrupted
  ## install, or a resolution change that reverted): resync the state file without a restart.
  if cmp -s "$ARGS_FILE" "$CAND_FILE" && cmp -s "$DRIVES_FILE" "$CAND_DRIVES_FILE"; then
    if ! cmp -s "$STATE_FILE" "$CAND_STATE_FILE"; then
      mv -f "$CAND_STATE_FILE" "$STATE_FILE"
    fi
    rm -f "$CAND_FILE" "$CAND_DRIVES_FILE" "$CAND_STATE_FILE"
    continue
  fi

  ## The new command line is logged by the hd-idle run script after the restart; unchanged ticks log nothing.
  bashio::log.info "Drive device paths changed – updating the hd-idle configuration and restarting hd-idle"
  ## Keep the previous drives file for hd-idle-pmfix (--since): only NEW or CHANGED drives get the (possibly
  ## wake-causing) treatment re-applied.
  cp "$DRIVES_FILE" "${DRIVES_FILE}.prev" 2>/dev/null || true
  mv -f "$CAND_FILE" "$ARGS_FILE"
  mv -f "$CAND_DRIVES_FILE" "$DRIVES_FILE"
  ## State file last: the commit point of the three-file install (records the shas just installed); a crash before
  ## it leaves the shas mismatching, and the next tick re-syncs.
  mv -f "$CAND_STATE_FILE" "$STATE_FILE"
  ## Unconditional: the pm-flag column carries the effective per-drive decision; pmfix skips pm-flag-0 drives.
  /usr/bin/hd-idle-pmfix "$DRIVES_FILE" --since "${DRIVES_FILE}.prev" \

## Drive inventory

The startup inventory (non-quiet `hd-idle-genargs` run only) maps every `sd*` disk to its model, first by-id link and
the label of its first labeled partition: filesystem label preferred (`/dev/disk/by-label`), GPT partition label as
fallback (`by-partlabel`), both shown when they differ; partitions are ordered by start sector
(`/sys/block/sdX/sdXN/start`); an unpartitioned disk shows its whole-disk filesystem label; a drive with no labeled
partition shows no label. Purely display output – nothing enters the args/drives/baseline files, so relabeling a
partition never triggers a watcher regeneration.

- The udev symlink trees are readable without any device-node access (device-access mechanics: §"Device access in this
  app") – reading symlinks cannot wake a standby drive. Superblock probing (`blkid`/`lsblk`) is NOT a viable label
  source: unlisted drives have no cgroup device access, and a superblock read spins up standby drives at every app
  (re)start.
- udev escapes bytes outside its safe set in by-label/by-partlabel link names as `\xNN` (space → `\x20`; observed on
  udev 259 – re-verify on the device's HAOS per the version-sensitive-facts rule); the inventory decodes them for
  display and passes raw names through unchanged.
- Duplicate filesystem labels (cloned drives): udev keeps only the first by-label link – the second drive shows no label
  (the inventory is an identification aid, not authoritative).
- LUKS/dm: a filesystem label on the unlocked volume points at the dm node and is not attributed to the holding
  partition; the container partition's GPT partlabel still is.

## Daemon failure semantics

The daemon is crash-only, with two fatal paths (v1.22 source): a `log.Fatal` when `/proc/diskstats` cannot be opened or
scanned (`diskstats/snapshot.go`), and a `log.Fatal` when the activity log `/data/hd-idle.log` cannot be opened or
written (`logToFile` in `hdidle.go`) – a full or read-only `/data` kills the daemon rather than disabling logging.
s6-supervise restarts the process in both cases, so a *persistent* failure becomes a crash loop that process supervision
cannot distinguish from a healthy app. The Docker HEALTHCHECK is the only container-level signal: `hd-idle-healthcheck`
re-checks both premises (stats file readable; daemon process alive via a `/proc/*/comm` scan) – the file probe covers
diskstats loss, the process probe covers both crash loops. The supervisor relays the resulting health events as bus
events and its app watchdog decides on a restart (root `KNOWLEDGE.md` §"Supervisor: health events and the app
watchdog"). Sources: [snapshot.go](https://github.com/adelolmo/hd-idle/blob/v1.22/diskstats/snapshot.go),
[hdidle.go](https://github.com/adelolmo/hd-idle/blob/v1.22/hdidle.go).

## SG_IO privileges

hd-idle opens disk nodes **O_RDONLY** (`sgio/common.go`, gated by `SG_GET_VERSION_NUM`) and issues `SG_IO` ioctls.
Kernel-side (`drivers/scsi/scsi_ioctl.c` `scsi_cmd_allowed()`, verified against master 2026-10; re-verify against the
device's kernel, 6.18-haos, before relying on it for new work): **START STOP UNIT (0x1B) is "read-safe"** – any process
that can open the node, no capability, no write access; covers hd-idle's `scsi` command type entirely. **ATA
PASS-THROUGH (0x85/0xa1, the `ata` command type) needs `CAP_SYS_RAWIO`** ("root can do any command" branch): the sole
reason for `privileged: [SYS_RAWIO]`, unconditional because Jmicron-quirk USB bridges (supported since 1.21) and all
SATA disks need the `ata` path.

Two independent AppArmor gates, both must be open: (1) the SG_IO ioctl is mediated only via the file's r/w permission
(no per-command mediation until AppArmor 4; mechanism: repository-root `KNOWLEDGE.md` §"AppArmor: mediation and profile
mechanics") – `/dev/sd* rwk,` plus the `file,` blanket covers it; (2) the kernel's `capable(CAP_SYS_RAWIO)` check inside
`scsi_cmd_allowed()` is mediated by AppArmor itself (same root section) – both profiles need `capability sys_rawio,`.
Without (2) every ata-path command failed with EPERM despite the container capability: capable() returned false and
`scsi_cmd_allowed()` fell through to `default: return false` (the EPERM source for O_RDONLY fds).

**Why the capability cannot be tightened**: AppArmor capability rules enumerate whole capabilities (they mediate the
kernel's boolean `capable()` check – apparmor.d(5)), so a fraction of `CAP_SYS_RAWIO` is not expressible; per-command
ioctl mediation does not exist upstream (root `KNOWLEDGE.md` §"AppArmor: mediation and profile mechanics"). **Both grant
sites are needed**: the daemon sub-profile (ata spindowns) and the top profile (pmfix's smartctl ATA SET FEATURES is the
same non-read-safe class; `hd-idle -t` runs in the top profile, e.g. the lab's `docker exec`). What the capability
additionally unlocks in this container (capabilities(7)): `/proc/kcore` reads (kernel-gated on capable(CAP_SYS_RAWIO),
file side allowed by the `file,` blanket – genuinely reachable for a compromised process; the accepted residual risk of
the ata path) and `ioperm`/`iopl` (x86/amd64). Closed surfaces: `/dev/mem`, `/dev/kmem`, `/dev/port`, `/dev/cpu/*/msr`
(outside the supervisor's device-cgroup allowlist); `mmap_min_addr` (moot: `/proc/sys` mounted read-only); SCSI commands
to other nodes (device cgroup); seccomp could trim further but the supervisor exposes no per-app seccomp customization.

## Device access in this app

Mechanics: repository-root `KNOWLEDGE.md` §"Supervisor: device access" (verified at supervisor ref 2026.11.0 – re-verify
per the version-sensitive-facts rule before relying on them for new work).

- Access is granted **exclusively via device-typed option fields**: `disks[].device` (`device(subsystem=block)`) –
  cgroup rules per configured drive, UI dropdown of stable by-id paths, hotplug re-grant via udev links (no restart
  needed on re-plug), system-disk refusal (exclusion layer 1). Hence every managed drive must be listed; unlisted drives
  are pinned to never spin down instead of being attempted.
- Saving options while a drive is detached fails, and so does every start: device existence is validated on EVERY start
  (root `KNOWLEDGE.md` §"Supervisor: device access").
- Plain Docker (the lab) exposes no `/dev/disk` udev symlink trees; the lab hook mirrors them (skill
  `ha-app-lab-testing`) so by-id resolution and inventory behave as on a device.

## Security rating ceiling

Formula, branches and sources: repository-root `KNOWLEDGE.md` §"Supervisor: app security rating". This app: 5 + 1
(custom profile) + 2 (no ports, no host network) − 1 (`SYS_RAWIO` is in the high-risk capability list) = **7 installed,
6 in the store listing**. `full_access` is deliberately avoided: rating 1, protection mode off, and cgroup access to
*all* devices including the system disk – which the device-option mechanism refuses precisely.

## hd-idle -t quirks

- The disk argument needs the **full `/dev/` path**: single-shot passes the argument straight to `openDevice` (the
  daemon path prefixes `/dev/`) – bare names fail (`open sda: no such file or directory`); the usage string's `-t sda`
  example is misleading.
- It uses hd-idle's **built-in defaults** for command type (`scsi`) and power condition (`0`) – verified against the
  v1.22 source (`main.go`, `defaultConf`), which matter because the app sets no global `-c`/`-p` (single-disk mode skips
  the per-device config entirely, so per-drive settings are ignored).

No in-app caller; the lab spindown smoke test drives it via `docker exec`, and it is useful for manual debugging.

## hd-idle-watch design

- **The problem**: hd-idle resolves its `-a` entries once at startup and `-s 1` re-resolves only still-unresolved ones,
  while kernel names (`sdX`) are not stable across re-plugs (ports/hubs, enumeration order): a moved drive keeps its
  stale entry – watched under the wrong name or none – until an app restart fixed it.
- **The supervisor cannot help**: its HARDWARE_NEW_DEVICE handling only re-grants cgroup device rules to the running
  container – no callback/notification API, no restart-on-device-change (verified against supervisor 2026.10.1). The fix
  is entirely app-internal.
- **Design**: arg generation lives in the shared helper `/usr/bin/hd-idle-genargs`; `hd-idle-watch` polls every 30 s
  (`HD_IDLE_WATCH_INTERVAL` override, floored at 5 s – the lab sets 5 s; mirrors nfsd-watch's `NFSD_WATCH_INTERVAL`):
  check first (baseline replay), and on a detected change regenerate into candidate files, compare, and install.
  Regenerated args AND drives matching the installed ones = only the baseline state is stale → resync without restart;
  otherwise install the candidates and restart just the hd-idle service (`s6-svc -r /run/service/hd-idle`). The state
  file (`<args-stem>.resolution`, e.g. `/etc/hd-idle.resolution`) is installed last (commit point – it records the shas
  of the two files just installed): a crash before it leaves the recorded shas mismatching the installed files, and the
  next tick re-syncs. Unchanged ticks log nothing; the new command line is logged by the hd-idle run script after each
  restart. Polling instead of udev events: mapping the host's `/run/udev` socket (`with_udev`) into an Alpine-based
  container is version-fragile for zero gain – 30 s worst-case latency is fine for a maintenance action.
- **Quiet mode and the baseline replay**: `--quiet` (the watcher's per-tick mode) suppresses narrative/info output and
  the expected-transient warnings (detached drive, non-sd\* entry) – both surface once per boot from the non-quiet
  cont-init run, and options cannot change mid-run (repository-root `KNOWLEDGE.md` §"Supervisor: option schema quirks");
  errors always log. `--check` (the nfsd-apply pattern, nfs-server commit d78c7ea) replays the **resolution baseline**
  the full generation recorded: the sha256 of each installed file plus the detection facts it was generated from
  (system-disk set; every configured device's resolution outcome – kernel name, `PASSTHRU`, or `IGNORED`), with no
  option reads, no jq, no file writes. Exit 0 = unchanged, 3 = changed (regeneration due), any other nonzero = check
  failure (the watcher keeps the current configuration: args file plus running argv, untouched). Because options are
  immutable mid-run, the recorded facts fully determine a regeneration; installed-file drift (hand edits, corruption,
  interrupted install) is caught by the shas – detection-equivalent to a full regenerate-and-compare. The state file is
  written LAST by the generation (commit point); its name derivation mirrors the drives file (`companion_file`, mirrored
  inline in the watcher run script).
- **Restart effects are benign**: the run script re-reads the args file; hd-idle starts with fresh in-memory stats (idle
  timers restart) and sends no command at startup – a drive in standby is NOT spun up by the restart. Cosmetic: an
  activity-log "running" period spanning the restart is misaccounted.
- **The clean upstream fix** would make the watcher redundant: re-verify already-resolved symlinks each cycle in `-s 1`
  mode and update changed entries (`TODO.md`); remove the watcher when upstream ships the behavior (Alpine package users
  get it via a package version bump + app version bump).
- **The failure class is nearly empty by construction**: options cannot change under a running app (the supervisor
  validates at save time and hands over new options.json only at the app's next start) – all config-content rejections
  fire at boot; device-resolution failures are not failures (passthrough path). The one reachable mid-run failure: two
  configured symlink names of the same physical drive (drives can carry several by-id links, e.g. `ata-*` and `usb-*`
  for one disk) with one detached at boot – the duplicate-entry rejection fires per tick (ERROR lines every 30 s until
  the user fixes the config; spammy but truthful, accepted). Known-good = the args file plus the running daemon's argv,
  both untouched on failure; the persistent source of truth is `options.json` on /data.

## Deploy tasks: local builds and store-copy conflicts

With a top-level `image:` key set, the supervisor **pulls that image from GHCR** instead of building the app folder
locally – an image-based app never rebuilds from source (see the [dev docs on testing on a
device](https://contributors.home-assistant.io/apps/guides/testing/#a-real-device)). The repo's device deploy tasks
(`deploy:local`, and `test:live` through it) therefore comment the key out in the *device-side* copy of the app's
`config.yaml`.

Two installations of the same app cannot coexist on one device – they conflict on the app's published ports. A
repository-installed copy (hashed store slug: §"Supervisor: store slugs (in-app documentation links)") therefore makes
`deploy:local` refuse: uninstall it first (the error message shows the exact `ha apps uninstall` command) or pass
`--replace` to have the task uninstall it automatically. `deploy:registry` switches a device from a local install by
uninstalling it, but refuses while a local and a repository-installed copy both exist (no flag – uninstall one by hand).
Whether a device can build at all depends on its DNS chain – see §"Supervisor: DNS resolution chain (CoreDNS)".

## Supervisor: ha CLI HTTP client timeouts

Every `ha` CLI API call is capped by a hard-coded per-command HTTP client timeout – no flag or env var overrides it
(home-assistant/cli `client/helper.go`, ref `bf6d59f`, checked 2026-11-02): commands using plain `GetJSONRequest()` get
**30 s** (`DefaultTimeout` – among them `ha apps start`), container operations (`apps restart/stop/uninstall/ rebuild`,
`core start/stop/check`…) get **10 min** (`ContainerOperationTimeout`), and downloads (`apps install/ update`, plugin/OS
=== ssh-ha.sh ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#MISE hide=true
#MISE description="⚠️ internal helper (sourced by device tasks, not runnable on its own)"
# Sourced by the device tasks (see .agents/skills/ha-app-device-testing): call `ha_connect <host-arg>` right after
# sourcing – it sets the contract variables `host` + SSH_OPTS that the other helpers read.

# shellcheck shell=bash
# shellcheck disable=SC2154  # host + SSH_OPTS are set by ha_connect
# shellcheck disable=SC2029  # the remote commands intentionally embed client-side values (function args)

ha_connect() { # ha_connect <host>: set the contract variables - normalize the SSH target (bare host -> root@: HAOS device
  # access is root-based) and SSH_OPTS
  host="$1"
  case "$host" in *@*) ;; *) host="root@$host" ;; esac
  SSH_OPTS=(-o ConnectTimeout=10)
}

ha_app_slug() { # ha_app_slug <app>: the app's slug from its repo config.yaml (fails when the repo has no such app directory)
  [ -d "$1" ] || {
    echo "ERROR: no app directory '$1' in the repo" >&2
    return 1
  }
  yq -r '.slug' "$1/config.yaml"
}

# The supervisor may still be settling after a device reboot (transient "not ready" /
# "is shutdown" messages from the ha CLI): wait up front, retry the mutators below on those.
wait_supervisor() { # poll until the supervisor API answers
  local n=1 probe rc
  while true; do
    # '|| rc=$?' keeps the probe out of errexit so the failure stays inspectable
    probe=$(ssh "${SSH_OPTS[@]}" "$host" \
      "ha supervisor info --raw-json 2>&1 | jq -e '.result == \"ok\"' >/dev/null" 2>&1) && rc=0 || rc=$?
    [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && return 0
    if [ "$rc" -eq 255 ]; then
      # rc=255 = ssh itself failed (network/auth) – no retry can fix that
      echo "ERROR: cannot ssh to $host: ${probe:-<no output>}" >&2
      return 1
    fi
    [ "$n" -lt 30 ] || {
      echo "ERROR: supervisor on $host not ready after 3 min (last probe: ${probe:-<no output>})" >&2
      return 1
    }
    echo "-- waiting for the supervisor to become ready ($n/30)"
    n=$((n + 1))
    sleep 6
  done
}

ha_retry() { # ha_retry <timeout-s> <cmd...>: retry commands failing with known transient messages
  local deadline=$((SECONDS + $1))
  shift
  local out rc
  while true; do
    out=$("$@" 2>&1) && rc=0 || rc=$?
    if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
      printf '%s\n' "$out"
      return 0
    fi
    if ! grep -qiE "not ready|is starting|is shutdown|connection refused" <<<"$out"; then
      printf '%s\n' "$out" >&2
      return "$rc"
    fi
    [ "$SECONDS" -lt "$deadline" ] || {
      printf '%s\n' "$out" >&2
      return "$rc"
    }
    echo "-- transient supervisor failure, retrying: $(head -c 120 <<<"$out")"
    sleep 5
  done
}

# 'ha apps start' cannot start slow apps: the CLI caps every API call with a hard-coded 30 s HTTP client timeout and
# offers no override (full timeout catalog: root KNOWLEDGE.md §"Supervisor: ha CLI HTTP client timeouts"). The
# supervisor holds the POST's response until the app reaches the started state, so POST it directly with a curl
# timeout we control (same pattern as ha_post_options below).
APP_START_TIMEOUT=300
ha_app_start() { # ha_app_start <slug>: start the app, tolerating slow startups (hd-idle's drive spin-up)
  local result rc
  result=$(ssh "${SSH_OPTS[@]}" "$host" \
    "curl -s --max-time ${APP_START_TIMEOUT} -H \"Authorization: Bearer \$SUPERVISOR_TOKEN\" \
      -X POST http://supervisor/addons/$1/start") && rc=0 || rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "ERROR: starting $1 failed or timed out after ${APP_START_TIMEOUT}s (curl rc=$rc) - the app may" >&2
    echo "       still be starting; check: ssh $host 'ha apps logs $1'" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  if ! echo "$result" | jq -e '.result == "ok"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    printf 'ERROR: the supervisor rejected starting %s: %s\n' "$1" "$result" >&2
    return 1
  fi
}

ha_ensure_running() { # ha_ensure_running <slug>: ensure the app runs after an install/update/restart ('ha apps install'
  # never auto-starts; updates/rebuilds only restart when it was running): start it when the state check finds it not
  # running, then verify again. Progress on stderr, final state on stdout (capture-safe); fails with a log hint when
  # the app still won't run.
  local state
  sleep 3
  state=$(ha_retry 120 ssh "${SSH_OPTS[@]}" "$host" "ha apps info $1 --raw-json" | jq -r '.data.state // empty')
  case "$state" in
    started | startup) ;;
    *)
      echo "-- app is not running (state: $state) - starting it" >&2
      ha_app_start "$1"
      sleep 10
      state=$(ha_retry 120 ssh "${SSH_OPTS[@]}" "$host" "ha apps info $1 --raw-json" | jq -r '.data.state // empty')
      case "$state" in
        started | startup) ;;
        *)
          echo "WARNING: the app state is '$state' even after a start attempt - check the app log:" >&2
          echo "         ssh $host 'ha apps logs $1'" >&2
          return 1
          ;;
      esac
      ;;
  esac
  printf '%s\n' "$state"
}

# --- supervisor REST probes -------------------------------------------------------------------

sup_get() { # sup_get <api-path>: supervisor REST GET (read-only), raw JSON
  ssh "${SSH_OPTS[@]}" "$host" \
    "curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer \$SUPERVISOR_TOKEN\" http://supervisor/$1"
}

sup_expect_ok() { # sup_expect_ok <api-path> <what>: sup_get + require result=="ok" - prints the raw JSON on success,
  # fails (with the response echoed) otherwise; readiness is established (wait_supervisor), so no retries
  local out
  out=$(sup_get "$1") || out=""
  if ! echo "$out" | jq -e '.result == "ok"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "ERROR: could not read $2 on $host: ${out:-<no output>}" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$out"
}

# The device resolves through the CoreDNS forward chain: manual servers, then the host's DHCP-learned DNS
# servers ("locals"), then the DoT fallback (root KNOWLEDGE.md §"Supervisor: DNS resolution chain (CoreDNS)").
# When the device's own IP is among them, whatever app serves :53 on the device sits in the device's own
# resolution path – a deploy task uninstalling that app (e.g. a hickory-dns copy) cuts the supervisor's DNS
# off, and the task's remaining DNS-dependent steps (registry downloads, store reloads, on-device builds)
# fail with a broken resolver on top.
device_resolves_through_self() { # 0 = the device's DNS servers include its own IP, 1 = no, 2 = undetermined
  local dns_info net_info own_ips resolvers
  dns_info=$(sup_get dns/info) || return 2
  net_info=$(sup_get network/info) || return 2
  # The device's own IPs: v1 nests the CIDR lists under .ipv4/.ipv6, v2 under .state/.config (both shapes
  # exist – root KNOWLEDGE.md §"Supervisor: DNS resolution chain (CoreDNS)").
  own_ips=$(jq -r '(.data.interfaces // [])[]
      | (.ipv4.address // []) + (.ipv6.address // [])
        + (.state.ipv4.addresses // []) + (.state.ipv6.addresses // [])
        + (.config.ipv4.addresses // []) + (.config.ipv6.addresses // [])
      | .[] | sub("/[0-9]+$"; "")' <<<"$net_info" 2>/dev/null) || return 2
  resolvers=$(jq -r '((.data.servers // []) + (.data.locals // []))[]
      | sub("^dns://"; "") | sub(":[0-9]+$"; "")' <<<"$dns_info" 2>/dev/null | sort -u) || return 2
  [ "$own_ips" != "" ] && [ "$resolvers" != "" ] || return 2
  local overlap
  overlap=$(comm -12 <(printf '%s\n' "$own_ips" | sort -u) <(printf '%s\n' "$resolvers"))
  [ "$overlap" != "" ]
}

# --- app options helpers (read-only probes skip ha_retry: readiness established, 'not installed' expected) ---

ha_app_options() { # ha_app_options <slug>: the install's current options as compact JSON ('' when none/unreadable)
  ssh "${SSH_OPTS[@]}" "$host" "ha apps info $1 --raw-json" 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -c '.data.options // empty' 2>/dev/null || true
}

ha_post_options() { # ha_post_options <slug> <options-json>: POST {options: ...}; fails on supervisor rejection
  local result
  result=$(printf '{"options": %s}' "$2" | ssh "${SSH_OPTS[@]}" "$host" \
    "curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer \$SUPERVISOR_TOKEN\" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      -X POST --data-binary @- http://supervisor/addons/$1/options")
  if ! echo "$result" | jq -e '.result == "ok"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    printf 'supervisor rejected the options: %s\n' "$result" >&2
    return 1
  fi
}

ha_schema_keys() { # ha_schema_keys <slug>: the app's schema keys as a JSON array (the info endpoint's schema field is
  # an array of {name, ...} objects or a key->spec object – both shapes exist, device-verified 2026-10-16)
  ssh "${SSH_OPTS[@]}" "$host" "ha apps info $1 --raw-json" \
    | jq -c 'if (.data.schema | type) == "array" then [.data.schema[] | .name] else [.data.schema | keys[]] end'
}

#!/usr/bin/with-contenv bashio
# shellcheck shell=bash
set -euo pipefail

## The app's drive-PM treatment: disable the drives' own power management for pm-flag-1 drives-file lines –
## semantics, drives-file format, --since and concurrency: hd-idle/KNOWLEDGE.md §"Drive-PM treatment";
## user-facing behavior: DOCS.md.
##
## Usage: hd-idle-pmfix <drives-file> [--since <old-drives-file>]

DRIVES_FILE="${1:-/etc/hd-idle.drives}"
SINCE_FILE=""

case "${2:-}" in
  --since)
    [ "${3:-}" != "" ] || {
      bashio::log.error "hd-idle-pmfix: --since needs a file argument"
      exit 1
    }
    SINCE_FILE="$3"
    ;;
  "") ;;
  *)
    bashio::log.error "hd-idle-pmfix: unknown argument '${2}'"
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

[ -r "$DRIVES_FILE" ] || {
  bashio::log.warning "hd-idle-pmfix: no drives file (${DRIVES_FILE}) – nothing to treat"
  exit 0
}

# Success detection (rc=0 AND no failed|unknown|unavailable output), the -d sat pin and timeout 60 – rationale:
# hd-idle/KNOWLEDGE.md §"Drive-PM treatment". The detail grep's different word list only picks a log line for the
# failure message, truncated to 80 chars: wide enough for full sense messages ("scsi error device will be ready
# soon"), still one short log line.
smart() {
  local dev="$1" flag="$2" value="$3" out rc attempt
  for attempt in 1 2 3 4; do
    if [ "$attempt" -gt 1 ]; then sleep 10; fi
    out=$(timeout 60 smartctl -d sat -s "${flag},${value}" "/dev/${dev}" 2>&1) && rc=0 || rc=$?
    if [ "$rc" = 0 ] && ! grep -qiE 'failed|unknown|unavailable' <<<"$out"; then
      if [ "$attempt" -gt 1 ]; then printf 'ok (attempt %s)' "$attempt"; else printf 'ok'; fi
      return 0
    fi
    # Retry filter: the NOT READY family only – timed-out and other failures never retry. Rationale (the rc alone
    # is too broad): hd-idle/KNOWLEDGE.md §"Drive-PM treatment".
    if [ "$rc" != 0 ] && grep -qiE 'will be ready soon|device not ready' <<<"$out"; then
      continue
    fi
    break
  done
  printf 'rc=%s (%s)' "$rc" "$(grep -aiE 'failed|unavailable|aborted|invalid' <<<"$out" | head -1 | sed 's/^smartctl [^|]*//;s/^ *//' | cut -c1-80)"
}

is_treated_before() {
  [ "$SINCE_FILE" != "" ] && [ -r "$SINCE_FILE" ] \
    && grep -qxF "$1" "$SINCE_FILE"
}

## Treatment targets: pm-flag-1 lines with a resolved sd* kernel name (a drive detached at boot appears under its
## by-id path and is skipped; the watcher's next cycle treats it under its resolved name). Treated drives dispatch
## to background jobs; each job writes its log line to a temp file numbered by drives-file order, logged after
## `wait` – the log stays deterministic despite the concurrent smartctl calls.
RESULT_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "${RESULT_DIR}"' EXIT
TREATED=0
while read -r name idle ctype pmflag; do
  [ "${name:-}" != "" ] || continue
  [[ "$name" =~ ^sd[a-z]+$ ]] || continue
  if is_treated_before "${name} ${idle} ${ctype} ${pmflag}"; then
    if [ "$pmflag" = "1" ]; then
      bashio::log.info "Drive ${name}: power management already disabled (unchanged configuration) – skipping."
    else
      bashio::log.info "Drive ${name}: drive-PM treatment disabled for this drive (configuration unchanged) – skipping."
    fi
    continue
  fi
  if [ "$pmflag" != "1" ]; then
    bashio::log.info "Drive ${name}: drive-PM treatment disabled for this drive – its own power management stays as is."
    continue
  fi
  TREATED=$((TREATED + 1))
  (
    apm=$(smart "$name" "apm" "off")
    stby=$(smart "$name" "standby" "off")
    printf 'Drive %s: APM disable %s; standby timer disable %s.\n' "$name" "$apm" "$stby" \
      >"${RESULT_DIR}/${TREATED}"
  ) &
done <"$DRIVES_FILE"
wait
for ((i = 1; i <= TREATED; i++)); do
  if [ -s "${RESULT_DIR}/${i}" ]; then
    bashio::log.info "$(cat "${RESULT_DIR}/${i}")"
  else
    bashio::log.warning "Treatment result ${i} missing – its concurrent job failed to record it."
  fi
done

#!/usr/bin/with-contenv bashio
# shellcheck shell=bash
set -euo pipefail

## hd-idle daemon (longrun service). Reads the generated argument list (/etc/hd-idle.args; written by cont-init
## config.sh, regenerated + restarted by hd-idle-watch when drive paths move; see hd-idle/KNOWLEDGE.md). `exec`
## makes hd-idle this service's process: s6 signals it directly on stop, and its stdout lands in the app log.

if [ ! -r /etc/hd-idle.args ]; then

fi
read -r -a HD_IDLE_ARGS </etc/hd-idle.args
bashio::log.info "Starting hd-idle: /usr/sbin/hd-idle ${HD_IDLE_ARGS[*]}"
exec /usr/sbin/hd-idle "${HD_IDLE_ARGS[@]}"

    SEEN_DEVICES["${NAME}"]=1
    ## The boot inventory already pairs each disk with its by-id link: a configured path that IS that link
    ## needs no separate mapping line (the common ata-* case); a different path (usb-*/wwn-*, /dev node,
    ## dm- holder) keeps its resolution line. The map stays empty in quiet runs – qlog_info no-ops there.
    DEV_LINK=${DEV#/dev/disk/by-id/}
    if [ "${INVENTORY_BYID[${NAME}]:-}" != "$DEV_LINK" ]; then
      qlog_info "Drive ${DEV} -> ${NAME}"
    fi
    record_resolution "$DEV" "$NAME"
    EMIT_NAME="$NAME"
  else
    ## Detached at startup: pass the path through for hd-idle's runtime resolution (-s 1; cgroup access is granted
    ## dynamically on hotplug); the watcher restarts hd-idle once it resolves (hd-idle/KNOWLEDGE.md §"hd-idle-watch design").
    qlog_warning "Drive '${DEV}' does not resolve right now (detached or still enumerating?) – passing it through for hd-idle's runtime resolution."
    record_resolution "$DEV" "PASSTHRU"
    EMIT_NAME="$DEV"
  fi

  if [ "$IDLE" = "0" ]; then
    qlog_info "Drive ${DEV}: idle time 0 – never spun down."
  fi
  ARGS+=(-a "$EMIT_NAME" -i "$IDLE" -c "$COMMAND_TYPE" -p "$POWER_CONDITION")

  ## Per-drive values for the drives-file line (format: hd-idle/KNOWLEDGE.md §"Drive-PM treatment");
  ## the 4th column is the drive-PM treatment flag.
  DRIVES_LINES+=("${EMIT_NAME} ${IDLE} ${COMMAND_TYPE} ${DRIVE_PM}")
done < <(echo "$DISKS")

if [ "$N_DRIVES" -eq 0 ]; then
  qlog_warning "No drives are listed – hd-idle will not spin down anything. Add the drives you want managed to the drive list (device access is granted per listed drive only)."
fi

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Global flags + command line output
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if bashio::config.true 'debug'; then
  ARGS+=(-d)
fi
if bashio::config.true 'ignore_spin_down_detection'; then
  ARGS+=(-I)
fi
if bashio::config.true 'activity_log'; then
  ARGS+=(-l "$LOG_FILE")
  qlog_info "Detailed activity log: ${LOG_FILE}"
fi

printf '%s\n' "${ARGS[*]}" >"$ARGS_FILE"
printf '%s\n' "${DRIVES_LINES[@]}" >"$DRIVES_FILE"

## Baseline state for the --check replay: shas of the two files just written plus the detection facts they were
## generated from. Written LAST – the commit point of the three-file install; a crash before it is re-synced next tick.
ARGS_SHA=$(sha256sum "$ARGS_FILE")
DRIVES_SHA=$(sha256sum "$DRIVES_FILE")
{
  printf '# hd-idle resolution baseline: written by hd-idle-genargs, replayed by its --check mode\n'
  printf 'args %s\n' "${ARGS_SHA%% *}"
  printf 'drives %s\n' "${DRIVES_SHA%% *}"
  if [ "${#SYSTEM_SD_DISKS[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
    printf 'system %s\n' "${SYSTEM_SD_DISKS[*]}"
  else
    printf 'system\n'
  fi
  for dev in "${RECORD_DEVICES[@]}"; do
    printf 'dev %s %s\n' "$dev" "${RECORD_RESOLVED[${dev}]}"
  done
} >"$STATE_FILE"
qlog_info "hd-idle command line: /usr/sbin/hd-idle ${ARGS[*]}"
qlog_info "hd-idle configuration completed"

if [ "${LIVE_HDIDLE_RENAME_DISK:-}" != "" ]; then
    live_rename_check || return 1
  fi
  return 0

live_rename_check() { # the port-move scenario (knob LIVE_HDIDLE_RENAME_DISK): the watcher's end-to-end promise.
  # Operator-paced: waits for the physical unplug + re-attach to a DIFFERENT port, then asserts – from the app
  # log alone (no docker CLI on the device: hook header) – the regeneration, the hd-idle service restart with
  # the drive re-resolved under its new kernel name, the hd-idle-pmfix decision on the changed drives-file
  # line, and a daemon-issued spindown under the new name (the device-access proof: the supervisor's hotplug
  # re-grant keeps the cgroup rules open for the renamed node without an app restart). The configured by-id
  # path (ata-* preferred: live_prepare) is stable across ports, so the drive keeps its configured identity;
  # only its kernel name changes. Moving the drive detaches it from every consumer – operator's choice.
  local disks_json="${LIVE_HDIDLE_DISKS_JSON:-}"
  if [ "$disks_json" = "" ]; then
    echo "-- rename scenario skipped: no managed drives in this run (set LIVE_HDIDLE_LABEL_GLOB so live_prepare includes drives)"
    return 0
  fi
  local selector="${LIVE_HDIDLE_RENAME_DISK:-}" rename_disk rename_label rename_dev rename_byid old_name new_name
  local logs after_change final_segment cmd_line expected pm_pattern pattern disk link_target
  local detected=0 found=0 spun=0 wait_start rename_delay
  local -a argv=() managed_arr=()
  local -r poll=15
  local -r rename_timeout="${LIVE_HDIDLE_RENAME_TIMEOUT:-1800}"
  local -r restart_window=180 event_window=420
  local detect_deadline=$((SECONDS + rename_timeout)) restart_deadline event_deadline

  ## Selector: a kernel name from the discovered map, or the filesystem label of exactly one included drive.
  rename_disk=$(jq -r --arg s "$selector" 'if has($s) then $s else empty end' <<<"$disks_json")
  if [ "$rename_disk" = "" ] \
    && [ "$(jq --arg s "$selector" '[to_entries[] | select(.value.label == $s)] | length' <<<"$disks_json")" = "1" ]; then
    rename_disk=$(jq -r --arg s "$selector" 'to_entries[] | select(.value.label == $s) | .key' <<<"$disks_json")
  fi
  if [ "$rename_disk" = "" ]; then
    echo "   FAIL: rename target '$selector' is neither a managed kernel name nor the label of exactly one included drive" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  rename_dev=$(jq -r --arg d "$rename_disk" '.[$d].device' <<<"$disks_json")
  rename_byid=${rename_dev#/dev/disk/by-id/}
  rename_label=$(jq -r --arg d "$rename_disk" '.[$d].label' <<<"$disks_json")
  old_name=$rename_disk

  echo "-- port-move scenario: the watcher's end-to-end promise (hd-idle/KNOWLEDGE.md §\"hd-idle-watch design\")"
  echo "   >>> MOVE THE DRIVE NOW: unplug '$old_name' (label '$rename_label', $rename_dev) and attach it to a"
  echo "   >>> DIFFERENT port on the device. Waiting up to ${rename_timeout}s."
  echo "   (the watcher picks the change up on its next tick, <=30 s after the re-attach)"

  ## Rename detection via the configured by-id link: udev removes it while the drive is detached and re-creates
  ## it with the new target when the drive comes back; a link still naming the old kernel name keeps waiting.
  while [ "$SECONDS" -lt "$detect_deadline" ]; do
    link_target=$(ssh -n "${LIVE_SSH_OPTS[@]}" "$LIVE_HOST" \
      "readlink '/dev/disk/by-id/$rename_byid' 2>/dev/null") || link_target=""
    link_target=${link_target##*/}
    if [ "$link_target" != "" ] && [ "$link_target" != "$old_name" ]; then
      new_name=$link_target
      detected=1
      wait_start=$SECONDS
      break
    fi
    sleep "$poll"
  done
  if [ "$detected" != 1 ]; then
    echo "   FAIL: no port move observed within ${rename_timeout}s (by-id link now: ${link_target:-absent})" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  echo "   rename detected: $old_name -> $new_name"

  ## Expected post-restart managed set: every managed drive under its current kernel name (the moved drive
  ## under its NEW one) – equality with this set also proves the stale name is no longer managed.
  expected=$(jq -cr --arg old "$old_name" --arg new "$new_name" \
    'keys | map(if . == $old then $new else . end) | sort | join(" ")' <<<"$disks_json")

  ## Wait for the watcher's regeneration and restart. The region is cut at the LAST "Drive device paths
  ## changed" line (the watcher logs it right before installing the candidates and restarting the hd-idle
  ## service); a service restart runs no cont-init, so the run script's "Starting hd-idle:" line – not
  ## "Configuring hd-idle..." – is the boot anchor, and it carries the full new command line.
  restart_deadline=$((wait_start + restart_window))
  while [ "$SECONDS" -lt "$restart_deadline" ]; do
    logs=$(ssh -n "${LIVE_SSH_OPTS[@]}" "$LIVE_HOST" \
      "ha apps logs $LIVE_LOCAL_SLUG --boot 0 --lines 400" 2>/dev/null) || logs=""
    after_change=$(awk '/Drive device paths changed/{buf=""} {buf = buf $0 "\n"} END {printf "%s", buf}' <<<"$logs")
    final_segment=$(awk '/Starting hd-idle:/{buf=""} {buf = buf $0 "\n"} END {printf "%s", buf}' <<<"$after_change")
    if [ "$after_change" != "$logs" ] && grep -q "symlinkPolicy=" <<<"$final_segment"; then
      cmd_line=$(grep -m1 "Starting hd-idle:" <<<"$final_segment" | sed 's|^.*Starting hd-idle: /usr/sbin/hd-idle ||')
      read -ra argv <<<"$cmd_line"
      managed_arr=()
      for i in "${!argv[@]}"; do
        [ "${argv[$i]}" = "-a" ] || continue
        managed_arr+=("${argv[$((i + 1))]}")
      done
      if [ "$(printf '%s\n' "${managed_arr[@]}" | sort | paste -sd' ' -)" = "$expected" ]; then
        found=1
        rename_delay=$((SECONDS - wait_start))
        break
      fi
    fi
    sleep "$poll"
  done
  if [ "$found" != 1 ]; then
    echo "   FAIL: no hd-idle restart with the new configuration within ${restart_window}s after the rename" >&2
    echo "         (the watcher did not pick up the changed resolution?); app log tail:" >&2
    tail -15 <<<"${final_segment:-$logs}" | sed 's/^/         /' >&2
    return 1
  fi
  echo "   PASS: hd-idle restarted with the new configuration (${rename_delay}s after the rename was detected –"
  echo "         the watcher's <=30 s tick plus regeneration) and manages exactly: $expected"

  ## hd-idle-pmfix on the changed drives-file line: the renamed drive's row is NEW for --since (the unplug
  ## cycle recorded its by-id passthrough row), so its decision re-applies exactly as at boot; every
  ## unchanged drive must be skipped by the --since diff (the redundant-treatment guard). Dash-free patterns
  ## – the log strings' dash normalization must not couple the assertions to one app version.
  if [ "$(jq -r --arg d "$rename_disk" '.[$d].pm_optout // false' <<<"$disks_json")" = "true" ]; then
    pm_pattern="Drive ${new_name}: drive-PM treatment disabled for this drive"
  else
    pm_pattern="Drive ${new_name}: APM disable"
  fi
  if ! grep -qF "$pm_pattern" <<<"$after_change"; then
    echo "   FAIL: no hd-idle-pmfix decision logged for the renamed drive ('$pm_pattern ...')" >&2
    tail -10 <<<"$after_change" | sed 's/^/         /' >&2
    return 1
  fi
  echo "   PASS: hd-idle-pmfix re-evaluated the changed drives-file line ('$pm_pattern ...')"
  while IFS= read -r disk; do
    [ "$disk" != "" ] || continue
    [ "$disk" = "$old_name" ] && continue
    if [ "$(jq -r --arg d "$disk" '.[$d].pm_optout // false' <<<"$disks_json")" = "true" ]; then
      pattern="Drive ${disk}: drive-PM treatment disabled for this drive (configuration unchanged)"
    else
      pattern="Drive ${disk}: power management already disabled (unchanged configuration)"
    fi
    if ! grep -qF "$pattern" <<<"$after_change"; then
      echo "   FAIL: no --since skip line for the unchanged drive ${disk} ('$pattern ...')" >&2
      echo "         (it must NOT be re-treated on a mere rename of another drive)" >&2
      return 1
    fi
  done < <(jq -r 'keys[]' <<<"$disks_json")
  echo "   PASS: --since skipped every unchanged drive (no redundant re-treatment)"

  ## The crown assertion: a daemon-issued spindown under the NEW kernel name proves the whole device-access
  ## chain (cgroup rules re-granted on hotplug, AppArmor SG_IO mediation, the node inside the container)
  ## kept working across the port move without an app restart.
  event_deadline=$((SECONDS + event_window))
  echo "-- waiting for a daemon-issued spindown of $new_name (idle 30 s, window ${event_window}s)"
  while [ "$SECONDS" -lt "$event_deadline" ]; do
    logs=$(ssh -n "${LIVE_SSH_OPTS[@]}" "$LIVE_HOST" \
      "ha apps logs $LIVE_LOCAL_SLUG --boot 0 --lines 400" 2>/dev/null) || logs=""
    after_change=$(awk '/Drive device paths changed/{buf=""} {buf = buf $0 "\n"} END {printf "%s", buf}' <<<"$logs")
    if grep -q "${new_name} spindown" <<<"$after_change"; then
      spun=1
      break
    fi
    sleep "$poll"
  done
  if [ "$spun" != 1 ]; then
    echo "   FAIL: no spindown event for $new_name within ${event_window}s of the rename pickup" >&2
    echo "         (device access not re-granted on hotplug? drive busy/no idle time?)" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  echo "   PASS: spindown event under the new kernel name – the device-access chain (cgroup rules plus"
  echo "         AppArmor) kept working across the port move without an app restart"
  return 0
}

Unit-tested the awk/jq/case logic locally against a synthetic log before running.
- by-id preference change (usb-first → ata-first): usb-* names carry an interface-instance suffix and can change across ports; ata-* derives from model+serial only — stable across ports/hosts/boots, and it matches the production config's ata-* references.    371	  local detected=0 found=0 spun_seen=0 wait_start rename_delay
   372	  local -a argv=() managed_arr=()
   373	  local -r poll=15
   374	  local -r rename_timeout="${LIVE_HDIDLE_RENAME_TIMEOUT:-1800}"
   375	  local -r restart_window=180 event_window=420
   376	  local detect_deadline=$((SECONDS + rename_timeout)) restart_deadline event_deadline

   381	    && [ "$(jq --arg s "$selector" '[to_entries[] | select(.value.label == $s)] | length' <<<"$disks_json")" = "1" ]; then
   382	    rename_disk=$(jq -r --arg s "$selector" 'to_entries[] | select(.value.label == $s) | .key' <<<"$disks_json")
   383	  fi
   384	  if [ "$rename_disk" = "" ]; then
   385	    echo "   FAIL: rename target '$selector' is neither a managed kernel name nor the label of exactly one included drive" >&2
   386	    return 1
   387	  fi
   388	  rename_dev=$(jq -r --arg d "$rename_disk" '.[$d].device' <<<"$disks_json")
   389	  rename_byid=${rename_dev#/dev/disk/by-id/}
   390	  rename_label=$(jq -r --arg d "$rename_disk" '.[$d].label' <<<"$disks_json")

   392	
   393	  echo "-- port-move scenario: the watcher's end-to-end promise (hd-idle/KNOWLEDGE.md §\"hd-idle-watch design\")"
   394	  echo "   >>> MOVE THE DRIVE NOW: unplug '$old_name' (label '$rename_label', $rename_dev) and attach it to a"
   395	  echo "   >>> DIFFERENT port on the device. Waiting up to ${rename_timeout}s."
   396	  echo "   (the watcher picks the change up on its next tick, <=30 s after the re-attach)"
   397	
   398	  ## Rename detection via the configured by-id link: udev removes it while the drive is detached and re-creates
   399	  ## it with the new target when the drive comes back; a link still naming the old kernel name keeps waiting.

   402	      "readlink '/dev/disk/by-id/$rename_byid' 2>/dev/null") || link_target=""

   406	      detected=1

   409	    fi
   410	    sleep "$poll"
   411	  done
   412	  if [ "$detected" != 1 ]; then
   413	    echo "   FAIL: no port move observed within ${rename_timeout}s (by-id link now: ${link_target:-absent})" >&2
   414	    return 1
   415	  fi
   416	  echo "   rename detected: $old_name -> $new_name"
   417	
   418	  ## Expected post-restart managed set: every managed drive under its current kernel name (the moved drive
   419	  ## under its NEW one) – equality with this set also proves the stale name is no longer managed.
   420	  expected=$(jq -cr --arg old "$old_name" --arg new "$new_name" \
   421	    'keys | map(if . == $old then $new else . end) | sort | join(" ")' <<<"$disks_json")
   422	
   423	  ## Wait for the watcher's regeneration and restart. The region is cut at the LAST "Drive device paths
   424	  ## changed" line (the watcher logs it right before installing the candidates and restarting the hd-idle
   425	  ## service); a service restart runs no cont-init, so the run script's "Starting hd-idle:" line – not

   430	      "ha apps logs $LIVE_LOCAL_SLUG --boot 0 --lines 400" 2>/dev/null) || logs=""

   434	      cmd_line=$(grep -m1 "Starting hd-idle:" <<<"$final_segment" | sed 's|^.*Starting hd-idle: /usr/sbin/hd-idle ||')

   436	      managed_arr=()
   437	      for i in "${!argv[@]}"; do
   438	        [ "${argv[$i]}" = "-a" ] || continue
   439	        managed_arr+=("${argv[$((i + 1))]}")
   440	      done
   441	      if [ "$(printf '%s\n' "${managed_arr[@]}" | sort | paste -sd' ' -)" = "$expected" ]; then
   442	        found=1
   443	        rename_delay=$((SECONDS - wait_start))
   444	        break
   445	      fi
   446	    fi
   447	    sleep "$poll"
   448	  done
   449	  if [ "$found" != 1 ]; then
   450	    echo "   FAIL: no hd-idle restart with the new configuration within ${restart_window}s after the rename" >&2
   451	    echo "         (the watcher did not pick up the changed resolution?); app log tail:" >&2
   452	    tail -15 <<<"${final_segment:-$logs}" | sed 's/^/         /' >&2
   453	    return 1
   454	  fi
   455	  echo "   PASS: hd-idle restarted with the new configuration (${rename_delay}s after the rename was detected –"
   456	  echo "         the watcher's <=30 s tick plus regeneration) and manages exactly: $expected"
   457	
   458	  ## hd-idle-pmfix on the changed drives-file line: the renamed drive's row is NEW for --since (the unplug
   459	  ## cycle recorded its by-id passthrough row), so its decision re-applies exactly as at boot; every
   460	  ## unchanged drive must be skipped by the --since diff (the redundant-treatment guard). Dash-free patterns
   461	  ## – the log strings' dash normalization must not couple the assertions to one app version.
   462	  if [ "$(jq -r --arg d "$rename_disk" '.[$d].pm_optout // false' <<<"$disks_json")" = "true" ]; then
   463	    pm_pattern="Drive ${new_name}: drive-PM treatment disabled for this drive"
   464	  else
   465	    pm_pattern="Drive ${new_name}: APM disable"
   466	  fi
   467	  if ! grep -qF "$pm_pattern" <<<"$after_change"; then
   468	    echo "   FAIL: no hd-idle-pmfix decision logged for the renamed drive ('$pm_pattern ...')" >&2
   469	    tail -10 <<<"$after_change" | sed 's/^/         /' >&2
   470	    return 1
   471	  fi
   472	  echo "   PASS: hd-idle-pmfix re-evaluated the changed drives-file line ('$pm_pattern ...')"
   473	  while IFS= read -r disk; do
   474	    [ "$disk" != "" ] || continue
   475	    [ "$disk" = "$old_name" ] && continue

   477	      pattern="Drive ${disk}: drive-PM treatment disabled for this drive (configuration unchanged)"
   478	    else
   479	      pattern="Drive ${disk}: power management already disabled (unchanged configuration)"
   480	    fi
   481	    if ! grep -qF "$pattern" <<<"$after_change"; then
   482	      echo "   FAIL: no --since skip line for the unchanged drive ${disk} ('$pattern ...')" >&2
   483	      echo "         (it must NOT be re-treated on a mere rename of another drive)" >&2
   484	      return 1
   485	    fi
   486	  done < <(jq -r 'keys[]' <<<"$disks_json")
   487	  echo "   PASS: --since skipped every unchanged drive (no redundant re-treatment)"
   488	
   489	  ## The crown assertion: a daemon-issued spindown under the NEW kernel name proves the whole device-access
   490	  ## chain (cgroup rules re-granted on hotplug, AppArmor SG_IO mediation, the node inside the container)
   491	  ## kept working across the port move without an app restart.
   492	  event_deadline=$((SECONDS + event_window))
   493	  echo "-- waiting for a daemon-issued spindown of $new_name (idle 30 s, window ${event_window}s)"
   494	  while [ "$SECONDS" -lt "$event_deadline" ]; do
   495	    logs=$(ssh -n "${LIVE_SSH_OPTS[@]}" "$LIVE_HOST" \
   496	      "ha apps logs $LIVE_LOCAL_SLUG --boot 0 --lines 400" 2>/dev/null) || logs=""
   497	    after_change=$(awk '/Drive device paths changed/{buf=""} {buf = buf $0 "\n"} END {printf "%s", buf}' <<<"$logs")
   498	    if grep -q "${new_name} spindown" <<<"$after_change"; then
   499	      spun_seen=1
   500	      break
   501	    fi
   502	    sleep "$poll"
   503	  done
   504	  if [ "$spun_seen" != 1 ]; then
   505	    echo "   FAIL: no spindown event for $new_name within ${event_window}s of the rename pickup" >&2
   506	    echo "         (device access not re-granted on hotplug? drive busy/no idle time?)" >&2
   507	    return 1
   508	  fi
   509	  echo "   PASS: spindown event under the new kernel name – the device-access chain (cgroup rules plus"
   510	  echo "         AppArmor) kept working across the port move without an app restart"
   511	  return 0
   512	}

# Loaded Skill: ha-app-workflow (skill)

Change and release discipline for this Home Assistant apps repository – branching, Conventional Commits, lint gates, the single-version-per-branch release rule with changelogs, CI-as-source-of-truth, device-access policy, and the version-sensitive-facts rule. Use before making any change, commit, or release in this repo.

## Content

# Change and release workflow

## Before starting

- Check the current branch first (`git status`): **Always work on a branch named `agent-<topic>`**, create one if needed
  (based off of `main`, i.e. `git switch -c agent-<topic> main`).
- If work belongs on a branch but a stray commit already landed on `main`: move it
  (`git switch -c agent-…; git branch -f main <upstream-tip>`) and disclose it to the user.
- Never stage unrelated WIP: check `git status` before staging and add files explicitly.

## Commits

- Conventional Commits (`build`, `chore:`, `ci`, `docs:`, `feat:`, `fix:`, `perf`, `refactor`, `revert`, `style`,
  `test`); scope app changes (`fix(nfs-server): …`); one commit per logical unit.
- Final trailer line: `Assisted-by: Goose:<model-slug>` – the model name without provider prefix, e.g.
  `Assisted-by: Goose:glm-5.3-flash`.
- The commit-msg hook enforces the format; escape hatch `HK=0 git commit`.

## Before finishing a change

Run `mise run check` – lint plus validate; it is the same gate CI runs. Lint-stack details and scoped checking: skill
`ha-app-tooling`. Task usage: `mise run check --help`.

## App releases

- A working branch starting from `main` bumps `version` in `config.yaml` to a **single** next version (major, minor or
  patch by semantic versioning): the branch ships one version, not one per commit, and continuously expands that
  version's `CHANGELOG.md` entry until it lands on `main`.
- Transitory extra versions within the branch are fine where testing demands one (AppArmor profile changes are only
  re-applied on app *update*, never on rebuild; root `KNOWLEDGE.md` §"AppArmor: mediation and profile mechanics") –
  squash them back into the single version (config plus one merged changelog entry) before merging.
- CI enforces the rule: `.github/workflows/version-guard.yaml` fails when device-visible app files (`rootfs/`,
  `Dockerfile`, `config.yaml`, `apparmor.txt`, `translations/`) changed without a version bump – the Supervisor's update
  model makes a no-bump change a silent no-op that only repoints an already-published version tag. Exception: if the
  base version's GHCR tag was never published (its release's build/publish failed), the guard probes GHCR and passes –
  reusing the version then repoints nothing; unprovable fails closed. Changes to docs-only files (README, DOCS,
  CHANGELOG, KNOWLEDGE, TODO, `.agents/`), the per-app `.dockerignore` (it shapes the build context but never changes
  the image the device receives), and repo tooling do not require a version bump.

## CI/CD is the source of truth for what gets published

- Pushes to `main` build and publish images (`.github/workflows/builder.yaml`). If CI fails, fix the repo, not CI config
  – unless the CI config itself is wrong.
- Builder caveats: the init job needs `fetch-depth: 0` – the changed-files filter otherwise only sees the tip commit and
  silently skips multi-commit merges, so use regular merges instead of squash merges.
- The app `Dockerfile` must not pull from Docker Hub at build time (rule and rationale: skill `ha-app-scaffolding`).
- The lint workflow runs frenck's app linter natively (pinned source plus pypi requirements), not via its Docker action
  (whose Docker Hub image builds flaked with 504s and 429 runner-pool rate limits).
- In `.github/workflows/`, match GitHub users and bots by immutable user id, never by `login` (root `KNOWLEDGE.md`
  §"GitHub Actions: user identity matching").

## Device access

Testing against the real HA device over SSH only on explicit user request; otherwise hand the user exact commands to
run. On-device procedures: skill `ha-app-device-testing`.

## Version-sensitive facts

Supervisor schemas, s6-overlay layout, HAOS kernel configs and HA docs change frequently. Wherever such facts are
written down (`KNOWLEDGE.md`, comments, skills), cite the source (URL plus version/ref). Before relying on them for new
work, re-verify against the latest docs/source. Source reads are stamped `verified at <ref> (<date>)`, on-device checks
`device-verified <date>`.

## Design change proposals

When a fix reveals a design issue, diagnose hands-on first (strace, packet captures, a reproduction lab), then explain
root cause, options and trade-offs to the user before rewriting.

## Text files

Every text file ends with a final newline (the lint gate enforces it).

1	#!/usr/bin/with-contenv bashio
     2	# shellcheck shell=bash
     3	set -euo pipefail
     4	
     5	## The app's drive-PM treatment: disable the drives' own power management for pm-flag-1 drives-file lines –
     6	## semantics, drives-file format, --since and concurrency: hd-idle/KNOWLEDGE.md §"Drive-PM treatment";
     7	## user-facing behavior: DOCS.md.
     8	##
     9	## Usage: hd-idle-pmfix <drives-file> [--since <old-drives-file>]
    10	
    11	DRIVES_FILE="${1:-/etc/hd-idle.drives}"
    12	SINCE_FILE=""
    13	
    14	case "${2:-}" in
    15	  --since)
    16	    [ "${3:-}" != "" ] || {
    17	      bashio::log.error "hd-idle-pmfix: --since needs a file argument"
    18	      exit 1
    19	    }
    20	    SINCE_FILE="$3"
    21	    ;;
    22	  "") ;;
    23	  *)
    24	    bashio::log.error "hd-idle-pmfix: unknown argument '${2}'"
    25	    exit 1
    26	    ;;
    27	esac
    28	
    29	[ -r "$DRIVES_FILE" ] || {
    30	  bashio::log.warning "hd-idle-pmfix: no drives file (${DRIVES_FILE}) – nothing to treat"
    31	  exit 0
    32	}
    33	
    34	# Success detection (rc=0 AND no failed|unknown|unavailable output), the -d sat pin and timeout 60 – rationale:
    35	# hd-idle/KNOWLEDGE.md §"Drive-PM treatment". The detail grep's different word list only picks a log line for the
    36	# failure message, truncated to 80 chars: wide enough for full sense messages ("scsi error device will be ready
    37	# soon"), still one short log line.
    38	smart() {
    39	  local dev="$1" flag="$2" value="$3" out rc attempt
    40	  for attempt in 1 2 3 4; do
    41	    if [ "$attempt" -gt 1 ]; then sleep 10; fi
    42	    out=$(timeout 60 smartctl -d sat -s "${flag},${value}" "/dev/${dev}" 2>&1) && rc=0 || rc=$?
    43	    if [ "$rc" = 0 ] && ! grep -qiE 'failed|unknown|unavailable' <<<"$out"; then
    44	      if [ "$attempt" -gt 1 ]; then printf 'ok (attempt %s)' "$attempt"; else printf 'ok'; fi
    45	      return 0
    46	    fi
    47	    # Retry filter: the NOT READY family only – timed-out and other failures never retry. Rationale (the rc alone
    48	    # is too broad): hd-idle/KNOWLEDGE.md §"Drive-PM treatment".
    49	    if [ "$rc" != 0 ] && grep -qiE 'will be ready soon|device not ready' <<<"$out"; then
    50	      continue
    51	    fi
    52	    break
    53	  done
    54	  printf 'rc=%s (%s)' "$rc" "$(grep -aiE 'failed|unavailable|aborted|invalid' <<<"$out" | head -1 | sed 's/^smartctl [^|]*//;s/^ *//' | cut -c1-80)"
    55	}
    56	
    57	is_treated_before() {
    58	  [ "$SINCE_FILE" != "" ] && [ -r "$SINCE_FILE" ] \
    59	    && grep -qxF "$1" "$SINCE_FILE"
    60	}
    61	
    62	## Treatment targets: pm-flag-1 lines with a resolved sd* kernel name (a drive detached at boot appears under its
    63	## by-id path and is skipped; the watcher's next cycle treats it under its resolved name). Treated drives dispatch
    64	## to background jobs; each job writes its log line to a temp file numbered by drives-file order, logged after
    65	## `wait` – the log stays deterministic despite the concurrent smartctl calls.
    66	RESULT_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
    67	trap 'rm -rf "${RESULT_DIR}"' EXIT
    68	TREATED=0
    69	while read -r name idle ctype pmflag; do
    70	  [ "${name:-}" != "" ] || continue
    71	  [[ "$name" =~ ^sd[a-z]+$ ]] || continue
    72	  if is_treated_before "${name} ${idle} ${ctype} ${pmflag}"; then

    74	      bashio::log.info "Drive ${name}: power management already disabled (unchanged configuration) – skipping."
    75	    else
    76	      bashio::log.info "Drive ${name}: drive-PM treatment disabled for this drive (configuration unchanged) – skipping."
    77	    fi
    78	    continue
    79	  fi
    80	  if [ "$pmflag" != "1" ]; then
    81	    bashio::log.info "Drive ${name}: drive-PM treatment disabled for this drive – its own power management stays as is."
    82	    continue
    83	  fi
    84	  TREATED=$((TREATED + 1))
    85	  (
    86	    apm=$(smart "$name" "apm" "off")
    87	    stby=$(smart "$name" "standby" "off")
    88	    printf 'Drive %s: APM disable %s; standby timer disable %s.\n' "$name" "$apm" "$stby" \
    89	      >"${RESULT_DIR}/${TREATED}"
    90	  ) &
    91	done <"$DRIVES_FILE"

    93	for ((i = 1; i <= TREATED; i++)); do

    95	    bashio::log.info "$(cat "${RESULT_DIR}/${i}")"
    96	  else
    97	    bashio::log.warning "Treatment result ${i} missing – its concurrent job failed to record it."
    98	  fi
    99	done

1	#!/usr/bin/with-contenv bashio
     2	# shellcheck shell=bash
     3	set -euo pipefail
     4	
     5	## Drive re-resolution watcher (longrun service): kernel names are not stable across re-plugs and hd-idle's -s 1 never
     6	## re-verifies already-resolved entries, so a moved drive would keep its stale entry until an app restart. Each tick
     7	## replays the recorded resolution baseline (hd-idle-genargs --check) and only on a detected change regenerates and
     8	## restarts just the hd-idle service. Problem, design, restart effects, failure class:
     9	## hd-idle/KNOWLEDGE.md §"hd-idle-watch design".
    10	
    11	## Poll interval (seconds); HD_IDLE_WATCH_INTERVAL overrides the 30 s default (the lab sets 5 s). Invalid values fall
    12	## back to the default, floored at 5 s so a bogus value cannot busy-cycle the tick.
    13	INTERVAL="${HD_IDLE_WATCH_INTERVAL:-30}"
    14	case "$INTERVAL" in
    15	  '' | *[!0-9]*)
    16	    bashio::log.warning "Invalid HD_IDLE_WATCH_INTERVAL '${INTERVAL}' – using the 30 s default."
    17	    INTERVAL=30
    18	    ;;
    19	esac
    20	[ "$INTERVAL" -ge 5 ] || INTERVAL=5
    21	
    22	ARGS_FILE=/etc/hd-idle.args
    23	CAND_FILE=/tmp/hd-idle-args.new
    24	## Companion files of the args file (derivation mirrored from hd-idle-genargs' companion_file; absolute paths here).
    25	DRIVES_FILE="${ARGS_FILE%.args}.drives"
    26	CAND_DRIVES_FILE="${CAND_FILE%.args}.drives"
    27	STATE_FILE="${ARGS_FILE%.args}.resolution"
    28	CAND_STATE_FILE="${CAND_FILE%.args}.resolution"
    29	
    30	while true; do
    31	  sleep "$INTERVAL"
    32	
    33	  ## Detect (read-only): 0 = unchanged, 3 = changed (regeneration due), other = check failure; mid-run failures are
    34	  ## nearly impossible by construction, so the keep-current guard is cheap insurance.
    35	  RC=0
    36	  /usr/bin/hd-idle-genargs --quiet --check || RC=$?
    37	
    38	  if [ "$RC" = 0 ]; then
    39	    continue
    40	  fi
    41	  if [ "$RC" != 3 ]; then
    42	    bashio::log.warning "Checking the hd-idle configuration failed – keeping the current configuration."
    43	    continue
    44	  fi
    45	
    46	  ## Regenerate from current options + current device resolution.
    47	  if ! /usr/bin/hd-idle-genargs --quiet "$CAND_FILE"; then
    48	    bashio::log.warning "hd-idle configuration regeneration failed – keeping the current configuration."
    49	    continue
    50	  fi
    51	
    52	  ## Regenerated args AND drives still matching the installed ones = only the baseline state is stale (interrupted
    53	  ## install, or a resolution change that reverted): resync the state file without a restart.
    54	  if cmp -s "$ARGS_FILE" "$CAND_FILE" && cmp -s "$DRIVES_FILE" "$CAND_DRIVES_FILE"; then

    56	      mv -f "$CAND_STATE_FILE" "$STATE_FILE"
    57	    fi
    58	    rm -f "$CAND_FILE" "$CAND_DRIVES_FILE" "$CAND_STATE_FILE"
    59	    continue
    60	  fi
    61	
    62	  ## The new command line is logged by the hd-idle run script after the restart; unchanged ticks log nothing.
    63	  bashio::log.info "Drive device paths changed – updating the hd-idle configuration and restarting hd-idle"
    64	  ## Keep the previous drives file for hd-idle-pmfix (--since): only NEW or CHANGED drives get the (possibly
    65	  ## wake-causing) treatment re-applied.
    66	  cp "$DRIVES_FILE" "${DRIVES_FILE}.prev" 2>/dev/null || true

    68	  mv -f "$CAND_DRIVES_FILE" "$DRIVES_FILE"
