1	#!/usr/bin/with-contenv bashio
     2	# shellcheck shell=bash
     3	set -euo pipefail
     4	
     5	## Generate the hd-idle command line from the app options (validated, written to <args-file>, default /etc/hd-idle.args)
     6	## for the s6 run script – hd-idle has no config file, everything is argv. Full generation (default) writes the args
     7	## file plus two companions: the drives file (hd-idle-pmfix) and the resolution baseline (the state file --check
     8	## replays: exit 0 = unchanged, 3 = changed (regeneration due), other = failure). CLI semantics, quiet-mode contract,
     9	## drives-file format, baseline replay: hd-idle/KNOWLEDGE.md.
    10	
    11	QUIET=0
    12	CHECK=0
    13	ARGS_FILE=""
    14	while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
    15	  case "$1" in
    16	    --quiet) QUIET=1 ;;
    17	    --check) CHECK=1 ;;
    18	    *) ARGS_FILE="$1" ;;
    19	  esac
    20	  shift
    21	done
    22	ARGS_FILE="${ARGS_FILE:-/etc/hd-idle.args}"
    23	LOG_FILE=/data/hd-idle.log
    24	
    25	qlog_info() {
    26	  [ "$QUIET" = 1 ] || bashio::log.info "$@"
    27	}
    28	
    29	## Expected-transient warnings (detached drive, non-sd* entry), suppressed in quiet mode – surfaced once per boot by
    30	## the non-quiet cont-init run; genuine failures (bashio::exit.nok) always log.
    31	qlog_warning() {
    32	  [ "$QUIET" = 1 ] || bashio::log.warning "$@"
    33	}
    34	
    35	## Every emitted token must be space-free: the run script word-splits the args file, so whitespace would corrupt the
    36	## argv. The supervisor schema blocks it for saved options; this covers hand-edited options.json.
    37	require_space_free() {
    38	  local what="$1" value="$2"
    39	  [[ "$value" != *[[:space:]]* ]] \
    40	    || bashio::exit.nok "Invalid ${what} '${value}': must not contain whitespace."
    41	}
    42	
    43	## Companion files next to the args file (<stem>.<suffix> for *.args paths, <args-file>.<suffix> otherwise – the
    44	## watcher's /tmp candidates). The derivation is mirrored inline in the hd-idle-watch run script.
    45	companion_file() {
    46	  local args_file="$1" suffix="$2" file
    47	  case "$args_file" in
    48	    *.args) file="${args_file%.args}.${suffix}" ;;
    49	    *) file="${args_file}.${suffix}" ;;
    50	  esac
    51	  [[ "$file" == */* ]] || file="./${file}"
    52	  printf '%s' "$file"
    53	}

    55	STATE_FILE=$(companion_file "$ARGS_FILE" resolution)
    56

    58	## Device resolution
    59	## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    60	
    61	## Parent block device of a partition name (sdi1 -> sdi, nvme0n1p2 -> nvme0n1). A trailing "p" is only stripped when
    62	## preceded by a digit, so genuinely named disks (e.g. "sdp") survive; whole-disk names like nvme0n1/mmcblk0 lose
    63	## their final digit – harmless, since only the sd* subset is ever pinned, recorded, or compared.
    64	parent_disk() {
    65	  local name="$1"

    67	  if [[ "$name" == dm-* ]]; then
    68	    printf '%s' "$name"
    69	    return
    70	  fi
    71	  while [[ "$name" =~ [0-9]$ ]]; do
    72	    name="${name%?}"
    73	  done
    74	  if [[ "$name" =~ [0-9]p$ ]]; then
    75	    name="${name%p}"
    76	  fi
    77	  printf '%s' "$name"
    78	}

    80	## Resolve a configured device value (by-* path, /dev node, or bare kernel name) to its kernel base name; returns 1
    81	## if the path does not resolve (e.g. drive currently detached).
    82	resolve_device() {
    83	  local dev="$1" target base holder
    84	  case "$dev" in
    85	    /dev/*)

    89	      fi

    91	      ## existence check a detached drive is misclassified as "not an sd* disk" and silently dropped from the
    92	      ## configuration instead of taking the pass-through path.
    93	      if [ ! -e "$target" ]; then
    94	        return 1
    95	      fi
    96	      base="${target##*/}"
    97	      ;;
    98	    *)
    99	      base="$dev"

   106	      [ -e "$entry" ] || continue
   107	      holder="${entry##*/}"
   108	      break

   111	      return 1
   112	    fi
   113	    base="$holder"
   114	  fi
   115	  printf '%s' "$base"
   116	}
   117	
   118	## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   119	## System disk detection (always on – HA's own partitions are never spun down)
   120	## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   121	
   122	## Three independent layers protect the system disk (hd-idle/KNOWLEDGE.md §"Monitoring scope"); this is the second:
   123	## the supervisor refuses system-used devices (1); the boot device and hassos-* partitions are pinned to idle 0 here,
   124	## first-match-wins (2); hd-idle only monitors sd*/dm-* anyway (3). Detection is set-based, order carries no semantics.
   125	
   126	## All detected system-disk base names (deduplicated) and their sd* subset.
   127	SYSTEM_DISKS=()
   128	SYSTEM_SD_DISKS=()
   129	ROOT_SOURCE=""
   130	
   131	## Dedup via an assoc array – this runs on every --check tick too, so keep it cheap.
   132	declare -A SYSTEM_SEEN=()
   133	add_system_disk() {
   134	  local parent
   135	  parent=$(parent_disk "${1}")
   136	  [ "$parent" != "" ] || return 0
   137	  [[ -z "${SYSTEM_SEEN[${parent}]+x}" ]] || return 0
   138	  SYSTEM_SEEN["${parent}"]=1
   139	  SYSTEM_DISKS+=("$parent")
   140	}
   141	
   142	detect_system_disks() {
   143	  ## The kernel command line's root= parameter (/proc/cmdline is not namespaced), resolved via the udev symlink trees
   144	  ## in /dev/disk. /proc/cmdline has no trailing newline: read exits nonzero at EOF – the words are assigned all the same.
   145	  local -a cmdline_words=()
   146	  read -r -a cmdline_words </proc/cmdline || true
   147	  local root_param="" root_link="" resolved="" word link disk
   148	  for word in "${cmdline_words[@]}"; do
   149	    case "$word" in
   150	      root=*) root_param="${word#root=}" ;;
   151	    esac
   152	  done
   153	  case "$root_param" in
   154	    UUID=*) root_link="/dev/disk/by-uuid/${root_param#UUID=}" ;;
   155	    PARTUUID=*) root_link="/dev/disk/by-partuuid/${root_param#PARTUUID=}" ;;
   156	    PARTLABEL=*) root_link="/dev/disk/by-partlabel/${root_param#PARTLABEL=}" ;;
   157	    /dev/*) root_link="$root_param" ;;
   158	    *) root_link="" ;;
   159	  esac
   160	  if [ "$root_link" != "" ] && resolved=$(readlink -f "$root_link" 2>/dev/null); then
   161	    add_system_disk "${resolved##*/}"
   162	    ROOT_SOURCE="root=${root_param}"
   163	  else
   164	    ROOT_SOURCE=""
   165	  fi
   166	
   167	  ## Every hassos-* partition sits on the system disk; partlabel resolution also covers setups where root= is unresolvable.
   168	  for link in /dev/disk/by-partlabel/hassos-*; do
   169	    [ -e "$link" ] || continue
   170	    resolved=$(readlink -f "$link")
   171	    add_system_disk "${resolved##*/}"
   172	  done
   173	
   174	  ## Only sd* disks can be pinned (hd-idle monitors nothing else; hd-idle/KNOWLEDGE.md §"Monitoring scope").
   175	  for disk in "${SYSTEM_DISKS[@]}"; do
   176	    if [[ "$disk" =~ ^sd[a-z]+$ ]]; then
   177	      SYSTEM_SD_DISKS+=("$disk")
   178	    else
   179	      qlog_info "System disk ${disk} detected – not an sd* device, hd-idle ignores it anyway."
   180	    fi
   181	  done
   182	  if [ "${#SYSTEM_SD_DISKS[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
   183	    qlog_info "Excluding the system disk(s) from spin-down: ${SYSTEM_SD_DISKS[*]} (${ROOT_SOURCE:+${ROOT_SOURCE}; }hassos-* partitions)"
   184	  elif [ "${#SYSTEM_DISKS[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
   185	    ## Boot-time concern only (cont-init warns once loudly); the watcher must not repeat it per tick.
   186	    qlog_info "Could not identify the system disk via root= or hassos-* partlabels. Only listed drives are ever touched; do not list the system disk."
   187	  else
   188	    qlog_info "System disk(s) identified but not sd* devices – hd-idle ignores them anyway."
   189	  fi
   190	}
   191	
   192	## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   193	## Baseline replay (--check): the watcher's per-tick detection
   194	## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   195	
   196	## The watcher's per-tick detection (nfsd-apply --check pattern, nfs-server commit d78c7ea): re-verify ONLY the
   197	## recorded detection facts – options cannot change mid-run, so if they all hold, the installed files are exactly
   198	## what a regeneration would produce. Exit 0 = unchanged, 3 = changed (resolution/system-disk drift or installed-file
   199	## drift), any other nonzero = check failure. Facts: hd-idle/KNOWLEDGE.md §"hd-idle-watch design".
   200	check_baseline_replay() {
   201	  ## No baseline (nothing recorded yet / boot not finished): regeneration due.
   202	  [ -s "$STATE_FILE" ] || return 3
   203	
   204	  local tag rest dev outcome sha
   205	  local recorded_args_sha="" recorded_drives_sha="" recorded_system=""
   206	  local -A recorded_resolutions=()
   207	
   208	  ## Line-based state format: 'args <sha256>', 'drives <sha256>', 'system <sd* names...>',
   209	  ## 'dev <configured device> <outcome>' (outcome: kernel name, PASSTHRU, or IGNORED). Device values are space-free
   210	  ## (require_space_free), so plain field splitting is safe.
   211	  while read -r tag rest; do
   212	    case "$tag" in
   213	      args) recorded_args_sha="$rest" ;;
   214	      drives) recorded_drives_sha="$rest" ;;
   215	      system) recorded_system="$rest" ;;
   216	      dev)
   217	        dev=""
   218	        outcome=""
   219	        read -r dev outcome <<<"$rest" || true
   220	        if [ "$dev" != "" ] && [ "$outcome" != "" ]; then
   221	          recorded_resolutions["${dev}"]="$outcome"
   222	        fi
   223	        ;;
   224	    esac
   225	  done <"$STATE_FILE"
   226	
   227	  ## The installed files must still be exactly what this baseline was generated from: this makes hand-edits,
   228	  ## corruption and partial installs (state file = commit point) detection-equivalent to a regeneration comparison.
   229	  [ "$recorded_args_sha" != "" ] && [ "$recorded_drives_sha" != "" ] || return 3
   230	  sha=$(sha256sum "$ARGS_FILE" 2>/dev/null) || return 3
   231	  [ "${sha%% *}" = "$recorded_args_sha" ] || return 3
   232	  sha=$(sha256sum "$DRIVES_FILE" 2>/dev/null) || return 3
   233	  [ "${sha%% *}" = "$recorded_drives_sha" ] || return 3
   234	
   235	  ## System-disk set drift: a re-enumeration can move the system disk's kernel name.
   236	  local -A recorded_system_set=()
   237	  if [ "$recorded_system" != "" ]; then
   238	    local -a recorded_system_fields=()
   239	    read -r -a recorded_system_fields <<<"$recorded_system" || true
   240	    for disk in "${recorded_system_fields[@]}"; do
   241	      recorded_system_set["${disk}"]=1
   242	    done
   243	  fi
   244	  [ "${#recorded_system_set[@]}" -eq "${#SYSTEM_SD_DISKS[@]}" ] || return 3
   245	  for disk in "${SYSTEM_SD_DISKS[@]}"; do
   246	    [[ -n "${recorded_system_set[${disk}]+x}" ]] || return 3
   247	  done
   248	
   249	  ## Per-device resolution drift: re-resolve every recorded device, compare the outcome class.
   250	  local current="" current_outcome=""
   251	  for dev in "${!recorded_resolutions[@]}"; do
   252	    if current=$(resolve_device "$dev"); then
   253	      if [[ "$current" =~ ^sd[a-z]+$ ]]; then
   254	        current_outcome="$current"
   255	      else
   256	        current_outcome="IGNORED"
   257	      fi
   258	    else
   259	      current_outcome="PASSTHRU"
   260	    fi
   261	    [ "$current_outcome" = "${recorded_resolutions[${dev}]}" ] || return 3
   262	  done
   263	
   264	  return 0
   265	}
   266	
   267	if [ "$CHECK" = 1 ]; then
   268	  detect_system_disks
   269	  RC=0
   270	  check_baseline_replay || RC=$?
   271	  exit "$RC"
   272	fi
   273	
   274	## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   275	## Configuration (full generation only)
   276	## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   277	
   278	DISKS=$(bashio::config 'disks')
   279	
   280	detect_system_disks
   281	
   282	## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   283	## Drive inventory (helps users map by-id paths and labels to kernel names)
   284	## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   285	
   286	## Boot-time UX only (non-quiet cont-init run). Since the --check baseline replay the watcher never
   287	## reaches this code; the guard just keeps the inventory out of regeneration ticks. Label sources,
   288	## escaping and known gaps: hd-idle/KNOWLEDGE.md §"Drive inventory".
   289	
   290	## udev escapes bytes outside its safe set in /dev/disk/by-* link names as \xNN (a space becomes
   291	## \x20); %b resolves exactly that escape alphabet and passes raw bytes through unchanged.
   292	decode_udev_name() {
   293	  printf '%b' "$1"
   294	}
   295	
   296	## Fill MAP (nameref) from the udev symlink tree DIR: resolved node's kernel name -> decoded label
   297	## (sda1, or the disk name itself for a whole-disk filesystem). Dangling links (vanished filesystems)
   298	## are skipped – the same staleness guard as the by-id scan in the inventory below.
   299	fill_label_map() {
   300	  local -n map=$2
   301	  local link target
   302	  for link in "$1"/*; do
   303	    [ -L "$link" ] || continue
   304	    target=$(readlink -f "$link" 2>/dev/null) || continue
   305	    [ -e "$target" ] || continue
   306	    # shellcheck disable=SC2034  # nameref: the write lands in the caller's map
   307	    map["${target##*/}"]=$(decode_udev_name "${link##*/}")
   308	  done
   309	}
   310	
   311	## Label fragment for one inventory line: the first partition in start order that carries a
   312	## filesystem label (preferred) and/or a GPT partition label (fallback; both shown when they
   313	## differ) – or, on an unpartitioned disk, the whole-disk filesystem label. Empty when nothing
   314	## is labeled. Reads sysfs and the label maps only: no device-node access, so standby drives
   315	## stay asleep (hd-idle/KNOWLEDGE.md §"Drive inventory").
   316	drive_label_info() {
   317	  local block="$1" name="$2" part_dir part start fs pl line
   318	  local -a parts=()
   319	  for part_dir in "${block}/${name}"[0-9]*; do
   320	    [ -d "$part_dir" ] || continue
   321	    part="${part_dir##*/}"
   322	    start=$(cat "${part_dir}/start" 2>/dev/null) || start=""
   323	    ## No readable start file: the sentinel sorts the partition last (cosmetic order only).
   324	    if [ "$start" = "" ]; then
   325	      start=999999999999
   326	    fi
   327	    parts+=("${start} ${part}")
   328	  done
   329	  if [ "${#parts[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
   330	    while IFS= read -r line; do
   331	      part="${line#* }"
   332	      fs="${FS_LABELS[$part]:-}"
   333	      pl="${PART_LABELS[$part]:-}"
   334	      if [ "$fs" = "$pl" ]; then
   335	        pl=""
   336	      fi
   337	      if [ "$fs" != "" ]; then
   338	        printf 'label (%s): %s' "$part" "$fs"
   339	        if [ "$pl" != "" ]; then
   340	          printf ', partlabel (%s): %s' "$part" "$pl"
   341	        fi
   342	      elif [ "$pl" != "" ]; then
   343	        printf 'partlabel (%s): %s' "$part" "$pl"
   344	      else
   345	        continue
   346	      fi
   347	      return 0
   348	    done < <(printf '%s\n' "${parts[@]}" | sort -n)
   349	  elif [ "${FS_LABELS[$name]:-}" != "" ]; then
   350	    printf 'label: %s' "${FS_LABELS[$name]}"
   351	  fi
   352	  return 0
   353	}
   354	
   355	## The by-id link the inventory shows per disk (filled in the non-quiet run): the configured-drive mapping
   356	## line in the configuration loop below is redundant when it names exactly this link.
   357	declare -A INVENTORY_BYID=()
   358	
   359	if [ "$QUIET" = 0 ]; then
   360	  declare -A FS_LABELS=() PART_LABELS=()
   361	  fill_label_map /dev/disk/by-label FS_LABELS
   362	  fill_label_map /dev/disk/by-partlabel PART_LABELS
   363	
   364	  qlog_info "Detected sd* disks:"
   365	  for block in /sys/block/sd*; do
   366	    [ -e "$block" ] || continue
   367	    name="${block##*/}"
   368	    model=$(xargs <<<"$(cat "${block}/device/model" 2>/dev/null || true)" || true)
   369	    byid=""
   370	    for link in /dev/disk/by-id/*; do
   371	      [ -L "$link" ] || continue
   372	      if [ "$(readlink -f "$link")" = "/dev/${name}" ]; then
   373	        byid="${link##*/}"
   374	        break
   375	      fi
   376	    done
   377	    labelinfo=$(drive_label_info "$block" "$name")
   378	    info=""
   379	    if [ "$byid" != "" ]; then
   380	      info="by-id: ${byid}"
   381	      INVENTORY_BYID["${name}"]="$byid"
   382	    fi
   383	    if [ "$labelinfo" != "" ]; then
   384	      info="${info:+${info}, }${labelinfo}"
   385	    fi
   386	    qlog_info "  ${name}: ${model:-unknown}${info:+ (${info})}"
   387	  done
   388	fi
   389	
   390	## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   391	## Drive configuration -> per-device entries
   392	## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   393	
   394	## The global idle stays pinned to 0: unlisted drives (and runtime-appearing ones) are never touched – HAOS grants
   395	## device access per listed drive only. Every drive entry carries explicit -i/-c/-p (its own settings; there are no
   396	## global defaults – the CLI's built-in defaults cover only what no entry reaches).
   397	ARGS=(-s 1 -i 0)
   398	
   399	DRIVES_LINES=()
   400	## System disks are exclusion entries (idle 0): never treatment targets, hence pm-flag 0; the command-type column is
   401	## "-" (no spin-down command is ever issued for them).
   402	for disk in "${SYSTEM_SD_DISKS[@]}"; do
   403	  DRIVES_LINES+=("${disk} 0 - 0")
   404	done
   405	
   406	for disk in "${SYSTEM_SD_DISKS[@]}"; do
   407	  ARGS+=(-a "$disk" -i 0)
   408	done
   409	
   410	N_DRIVES=0
   411	declare -A SEEN_DEVICES=()
   412	## Baseline records for the state file: every configured device (options order, deterministic) with its resolution
   413	## OUTCOME (kernel name / PASSTHRU / IGNORED) – fully determines the generated configuration given immutable options.
   414	RECORD_DEVICES=()
   415	declare -A RECORD_RESOLVED=()
   416	record_resolution() {
   417	  RECORD_DEVICES+=("${1}")
   418	  RECORD_RESOLVED["${1}"]="${2}"
   419	}
   420	
   421	## bashio::config returns one compact JSON object per line for list-of-object options
   422	## (hd-idle/KNOWLEDGE.md §"bashio option parsing (list-of-object options)").
   423	while IFS= read -r disk; do
   424	  [ "$disk" != "" ] || continue
   425	  N_DRIVES=$((N_DRIVES + 1))
   426	  DEV=$(bashio::jq "$disk" '.device')
   427	  IDLE=$(bashio::jq "$disk" '.idle // empty')
   428	  COMMAND_TYPE=$(bashio::jq "$disk" '.command_type // empty')
   429	  POWER_CONDITION=$(bashio::jq "$disk" '.power_condition // empty')
   430	  require_space_free 'device' "$DEV"
   431	  require_space_free 'idle' "$IDLE"
   432	  require_space_free 'command_type' "$COMMAND_TYPE"
   433	  require_space_free 'power_condition' "$POWER_CONDITION"
   434	  ## The supervisor schema marks idle/command_type/power_condition required, so an empty value here means a
   435	  ## hand-edited options.json. Defense in depth: cheap re-checks keep one from producing a bogus argv.
   436	  [ "$IDLE" != "" ] \
   437	    || bashio::exit.nok "Drive '${DEV}': missing idle time – every drive sets its own (0 = never spin down)."
   438	  [[ "$IDLE" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] \
   439	    || bashio::exit.nok "Drive '${DEV}': invalid idle time '${IDLE}': must be a non-negative integer."
   440	  [ "$COMMAND_TYPE" != "" ] \
   441	    || bashio::exit.nok "Drive '${DEV}': missing command type – every drive sets its own (scsi or ata)."
   442	  case "$COMMAND_TYPE" in
   443	    scsi | ata) ;;
   444	    *)
   445	      bashio::exit.nok "Drive '${DEV}': invalid command type '${COMMAND_TYPE}': must be scsi or ata."
   446	      ;;
   447	  esac
   448	  [ "$POWER_CONDITION" != "" ] \
   449	    || bashio::exit.nok "Drive '${DEV}': missing power condition – every drive sets its own (0–15)."
   450	  if ! [[ "$POWER_CONDITION" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || [ "$POWER_CONDITION" -gt 15 ]; then
   451	    bashio::exit.nok "Drive '${DEV}': invalid power condition '${POWER_CONDITION}': must be 0-15."
   452	  fi
   453	  ## Per-drive drive-PM opt-out (bool?), read WITHOUT `// empty` and matched strictly: jq folds an explicit false into
   454	  ## "absent" (root KNOWLEDGE.md §"bashio option consumption"). Absent (null) and false mean the same thing here – the
   455	  ## treatment applies (the default); true exempts the drive. Defense in depth like the re-checks above – the
   456	  ## supervisor normalizes bool options before the app ever sees them
   457	  ## (root KNOWLEDGE.md §"Supervisor: option schema quirks").
   458	  PM=$(bashio::jq "$disk" '.keep_drive_pm')
   459	  case "$PM" in
   460	    true) DRIVE_PM=0 ;;
   461	    false | null) DRIVE_PM=1 ;;
   462	    *)
   463	      bashio::exit.nok "Drive '${DEV}': invalid keep_drive_pm value '${PM}': must be true, false, or unset."
   464	      ;;
   465	  esac
   466	  ## Partition selection grants cgroup access only for the partition node, while hd-idle opens the disk node.
   467	  if [[ "$DEV" == *-part[0-9]* ]]; then
   468	    bashio::exit.nok "Drive '${DEV}' is a partition (by-id path ending in -partN): select the disk itself (the dropdown entry without -partN) – the app needs the whole disk."
   469	  fi
   470	
   471	  if RESOLVED=$(resolve_device "$DEV"); then
   472	    if [[ "$RESOLVED" =~ ^sd[a-z]+$ ]]; then
   473	      NAME="$RESOLVED"
   474	    elif [[ "$RESOLVED" =~ ^sd[a-z]+[0-9]+$ ]]; then
   475	      bashio::exit.nok "Drive '${DEV}' resolves to partition ${RESOLVED}: select the disk itself (the dropdown entry without -partN) – the app needs the whole disk."
   476	    else
   477	      qlog_warning "Drive '${DEV}' resolves to ${RESOLVED}, which is not an sd* disk – hd-idle cannot manage it; entry ignored."
   478	      record_resolution "$DEV" "IGNORED"
   479	      continue
   480	    fi
   481	    if [[ -n "${SYSTEM_SEEN[${NAME}]+x}" ]]; then
   482	      bashio::exit.nok "Drive '${DEV}' is the system disk Home Assistant runs from (${NAME}) – it is always excluded from spin-down and cannot be configured as a managed drive."
   483	    fi
   484	    if [[ -n "${SEEN_DEVICES[${NAME}]+x}" ]]; then
   485	      bashio::exit.nok "Drive ${NAME} (${DEV}) is configured more than once: one configuration per disk – remove the redundant entry."
   486	    fi
   487	    SEEN_DEVICES["${NAME}"]=1
   488	    ## The boot inventory already pairs each disk with its by-id link: a configured path that IS that link
   489	    ## needs no separate mapping line (the common ata-* case); a different path (usb-*/wwn-*, /dev node,
   490	    ## dm- holder) keeps its resolution line. The map stays empty in quiet runs – qlog_info no-ops there.
   491	    DEV_LINK=${DEV#/dev/disk/by-id/}
   492	    if [ "${INVENTORY_BYID[${NAME}]:-}" != "$DEV_LINK" ]; then
   493	      qlog_info "Drive ${DEV} -> ${NAME}"
   494	    fi
   495	    record_resolution "$DEV" "$NAME"
   496	    EMIT_NAME="$NAME"
   497	  else
   498	    ## Detached at startup: pass the path through for hd-idle's runtime resolution (-s 1; cgroup access is granted
   499	    ## dynamically on hotplug); the watcher restarts hd-idle once it resolves (hd-idle/KNOWLEDGE.md §"hd-idle-watch design").
   500	    qlog_warning "Drive '${DEV}' does not resolve right now (detached or still enumerating?) – passing it through for hd-idle's runtime resolution."
   501	    record_resolution "$DEV" "PASSTHRU"
   502	    EMIT_NAME="$DEV"
   503	  fi
   504	
   505	  if [ "$IDLE" = "0" ]; then
   506	    qlog_info "Drive ${DEV}: idle time 0 – never spun down."
   507	  fi
   508	  ARGS+=(-a "$EMIT_NAME" -i "$IDLE" -c "$COMMAND_TYPE" -p "$POWER_CONDITION")
   509	
   510	  ## Per-drive values for the drives-file line (format: hd-idle/KNOWLEDGE.md §"Drive-PM treatment");
   511	  ## the 4th column is the drive-PM treatment flag.
   512	  DRIVES_LINES+=("${EMIT_NAME} ${IDLE} ${COMMAND_TYPE} ${DRIVE_PM}")
   513	done < <(echo "$DISKS")
   514	
   515	if [ "$N_DRIVES" -eq 0 ]; then
   516	  qlog_warning "No drives are listed – hd-idle will not spin down anything. Add the drives you want managed to the drive list (device access is granted per listed drive only)."
   517	fi
   518	
   519	## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   520	## Global flags + command line output
   521	## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   522	
   523	if bashio::config.true 'debug'; then
   524	  ARGS+=(-d)
   525	fi
   526	if bashio::config.true 'ignore_spin_down_detection'; then
   527	  ARGS+=(-I)
   528	fi
   529	if bashio::config.true 'activity_log'; then
   530	  ARGS+=(-l "$LOG_FILE")
   531	  qlog_info "Detailed activity log: ${LOG_FILE}"
   532	fi
   533	
   534	printf '%s\n' "${ARGS[*]}" >"$ARGS_FILE"
   535	printf '%s\n' "${DRIVES_LINES[@]}" >"$DRIVES_FILE"
   536	
   537	## Baseline state for the --check replay: shas of the two files just written plus the detection facts they were
   538	## generated from. Written LAST – the commit point of the three-file install; a crash before it is re-synced next tick.
   539	ARGS_SHA=$(sha256sum "$ARGS_FILE")
   540	DRIVES_SHA=$(sha256sum "$DRIVES_FILE")
   541	{
   542	  printf '# hd-idle resolution baseline: written by hd-idle-genargs, replayed by its --check mode\n'
   543	  printf 'args %s\n' "${ARGS_SHA%% *}"
   544	  printf 'drives %s\n' "${DRIVES_SHA%% *}"
   545	  if [ "${#SYSTEM_SD_DISKS[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
   546	    printf 'system %s\n' "${SYSTEM_SD_DISKS[*]}"
   547	  else
   548	    printf 'system\n'
   549	  fi
   550	  for dev in "${RECORD_DEVICES[@]}"; do
   551	    printf 'dev %s %s\n' "$dev" "${RECORD_RESOLVED[${dev}]}"
   552	  done
   553	} >"$STATE_FILE"
   554	qlog_info "hd-idle command line: /usr/sbin/hd-idle ${ARGS[*]}"
   555	qlog_info "hd-idle configuration completed"

The skill references the hook contract generically — hook-local knobs are self-documented in the hook header, so nothing external breaks. My review is complete. Here's what I found in the three commits (plus adjacent drift the review surfaced):

**Findings**

1. **Bug (f8fb27d, phase 2): the rename check's managed-set parse counts system-disk exclusions as managed drives.** genargs emits `-a <system-sd> -i 0` exclusion entries; phase 1 correctly classifies idle‑0 entries as excluded, but `live_rename_check` collects **every** `-a` token. On any device whose HAOS boot medium is an `sd*` disk (e.g. a Pi with USB‑SSD boot), the equality `managed_arr == expected` can never hold → the scenario false-fails. It passed on 192.168.1.11 only because that box boots from a non-`sd*` medium.
2. **Dead anchor (predates, drifted in app 0.1.5):** `grep -q "No drives configured"` — the app logs `No drives are listed – …` since commit `1f5868a`; the "safe no‑op" PASS line can never fire.
3. **Operator trap (f8fb27d):** if a re-plug returns the drive under its **old** kernel name (kernels reuse free names), the hook waits out the full 1800 s silently — the one scenario where the watcher rightly does nothing goes undiagnosed.
4. **Label matching compares udev‑escaped names** (e.g. a space label arrives as `My\x20Movies`), so space-bearing labels can't be selected naturally; also labels are space‑split into fragments.
5. Cosmetic: "spundown" typo; `{label, device}` header doc misses `pm_optout`; implicit globals; awk cut idiom duplicated 4×; `-a` parse duplicated with drifting semantics (root cause of #1).

Now implementing the fixes, starting with the shared-parse refactor + phase‑2 bug:

# shellcheck disable=SC2029  # remote commands intentionally embed client-side values
# shellcheck disable=SC2034  # LIVE_* are the harness contract variables

## Log region after the LAST line containing <pat> (the whole log when it never matches – callers detect
## that by inequality). Literal-string anchors only: the awk uses index(), not a regex.
after_last_match() { # <pat> <log>
  awk -v pat="$1" 'index($0, pat) { buf = "" } { buf = buf $0 "\n" } END { printf "%s", buf }' <<<"$2"
}

## The -a entries of an hd-idle command line (genargs emits `-a NAME -i IDLE ...` per entry): one
## "<name> <idle>" line per entry – managed drives and idle-0 system-disk exclusions alike; the
## consumers classify by the idle value.
cmdline_a_entries() { # <cmdline>
  local -a argv=()
  local i
  read -ra argv <<<"$1"
  for i in "${!argv[@]}"; do
    [ "${argv[$i]}" = "-a" ] || continue
    printf '%s %s\n' "${argv[$((i + 1))]}" "${argv[$((i + 3))]:-}"
  done
}
